definition_zh: 怨恨；积怨；勉强给予；不情愿地做
definition_en: a lasting feeling of anger at someone for a past hurt, or to give something unwillingly
core_image: 心里压着一块沉甸甸的石头，因为上次的事一直不放下
scene: 她被当众批评之后，一直记着这件事，见面就沉着脸。She still bears a grudge against her old coach for that public criticism.
sceneCN: 这里 grudge 是「怨恨、积怨」（第 1 个义项：因旧事而长期记恨）；句意：她仍因那次当众批评而对老教练心怀怨恨。

derivatives.zh: 基础词加形容词词尾 -ing，义为「勉强的；不情愿的」
grudging 加副词词尾 -ly，义为「不情愿地」
基础词加施动者词尾 -er，义为「心怀怨恨的人」
前缀 be- + grudge，义为「嫉妒；舍不得」

senses.title: A lasting resentment
senses.definition: a strong feeling of anger at someone because of something that happened in the past
senses.definitionCN: 因过去发生的事而对某人怀有的强烈怒气
senses.example: He still bears a grudge against his former boss.
senses.exampleCN: 他仍对前任老板心怀怨恨。
senses.why: The old verb meant to murmur or complain, so the word starts as a complaint that will not fade.
senses.whyCN: 古义为嘟囔、抱怨，所以「怨」从一句不肯消散的抱怨开始。

senses.title: A reason for dislike
senses.definition: a cause or excuse for dislike or ill will
senses.definitionCN: 产生不喜欢或恶意的原因、借口
senses.example: She has a grudge against the school over the fees.
senses.exampleCN: 她因学费的事对学校心存不满。
senses.why: A grudge can name the thing itself that people hold against another, not only the feeling.
senses.whyCN: grudge 不仅能指情绪，还能指「被人记在心里的那件事」。

senses.title: To give unwillingly
senses.definition: to give or allow something with reluctance
senses.definitionCN: 不情愿地给予或允许
senses.example: He grudged every penny he spent on rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房租上的每一分钱他都掏得极不情愿。
senses.why: Old use meant to grant reluctantly, so the verb keeps the image of a hand that opens only slowly.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的意义是「勉强应允」，所以动词保留了那只慢慢松开的手的形象。

senses.title: To complain about in private
senses.definition: to murmur or complain about something quietly
senses.definitionCN: 低声抱怨某事、心里不满
senses.example: The men grudged the extra hours in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们默默地对多出来的工时心怀不满。
senses.why: The earliest sense was a low murmur, which survives as a private complaint about unfairness.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意义就是低声嘟囔，这一层以「私下抱怨不公」的形式留存下来。

senses.title: To begrudge another success
senses.definition: to feel envy about something another person has
senses.definitionCN: 嫉妒别人拥有的东西
senses.example: Nobody grudged her the prize she had earned.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭本事得来的奖，没有人嫉妒。
senses.why: If you give praise unwillingly, you are jealous, so the verb reaches envy through the prefix be-.
senses.whyCN: 连赞美都不情愿给，就是嫉妒，所以 begrudge 通过前缀 be- 延伸到嫉妒。

intro.en: Grudge comes from Old French grouchier, to murmur or grumble, which is probably a Germanic word of uncertain shape.
intro.cn: grudge 来自古法语 grouchier（嘟囔、抱怨），一般认为这是日耳曼语来源的词，具体形式不确定。

items.en: Grouchier is probably Germanic; the exact source is uncertain.
items.cn: grouchier 一般认为来自日耳曼语，确切来源不确定。

items.en: Grouchier means to murmur or be displeased.
items.cn: 古法语 grouchier 意为嘟囔、不满。

items.en: Grudge first means to murmur or grumble.
items.cn: 英语最先用 grudge 表示低声抱怨。

items.en: The noun grudge names a complaint or ill will.
items.cn: 名词 grudge 指抱怨或恶意。

items.en: The verb takes the sense to give unwillingly.
items.cn: 动词在十七世纪的英语里获得「勉强给予」义。

items.en: Bear a grudge becomes the dominant phrase today.
items.cn: 现代英语中以 bear a grudge 这一搭配最为常用。

note.en: Grudge sits beside begrudge and grudgingly, and near resentment, bitterness, and malice.
note.cn: grudge 与 begrudge、grudgingly 同族，与 resentment、bitterness、malice 义近。

entries.definition: to envy or give unwillingly
entries.definitionCN: 嫉妒；舍不得给

entries.definition: unwilling
entries.definitionCN: 勉强的；不情愿的

entries.definition: in an unwilling way
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿地

entries.definition: bitter anger at unfair treatment
entries.definitionCN: 怨恨；不满

entries.definition: lasting angry disappointment
entries.definitionCN: 苦涩；怨恨

entries.definition: a wish to harm others
entries.definitionCN: 恶意；坏心

normalIntro.en: Grudge works as both a noun and a verb, and its family branches out through grudge and begrudge.
normalIntro.cn: grudge 既是名词也是动词，词族通过 grudge 与 begrudge 等词延伸。

normal.en: The main noun phrase is bear a grudge against someone.
normal.cn: 主要名词短语是 bear a grudge against someone（对某人心怀怨恨）。

normal.en: Hold and nurse both go with grudge as verbs.
normal.cn: hold 和 nurse 都能与 grudge 搭配：hold a grudge、nurse a grudge。

normal.en: The adjective is grudging, as in a grudging apology.
normal.cn: 形容词是 grudging，如 a grudging apology（不情愿的道歉）。

normal.en: Begrudge adds be- and means to envy or stint.
normal.cn: begrudge 加上 be- 前缀，意为嫉妒或吝惜。

normal.en: The verb grudge takes a thing, not a person: he grudged the money.
normal.cn: 动词 grudge 接物不接人：he grudged the money（他舍不得这笔钱）。

abstract.en: Picture a stone kept in the chest that never gets set down.
abstract.cn: 想象胸口压着一块从不放下的石头。

abstract.en: See a hand that opens only a crack when asked for help.
abstract.cn: 看见别人求助时，那只手只肯裂开一条缝。

abstract.en: Imagine a low murmur behind a closed door after an argument.
abstract.cn: 想象争吵后紧闭的门后传来低低的嘟囔声。

examples.en: She bears no grudge against the team that beat her.
examples.cn: 她对打败她的队伍并不记恨。

examples.en: He grudged the time he had to spend on paperwork.
examples.cn: 他对不得不用在文书上的时间极不情愿。

examples.en: They blamed each other for years, nursing secret grudges.
examples.cn: 多年来他们互相指责，暗自抱着一肚子积怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「割路之」——心里那道被割出的路，一直在那儿隐隐作痛，走一次记一次仇；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 grouchier（嘟囔、抱怨，一般认为源自日耳曼语）→ 英语 grudge（低怨、不满）→ 「记恨」与「勉强给予」，核心义「压在心里的怨」。

sensesIntro.en: Grudge begins as a low complaint, becomes a lasting resentment, then the reason for it, the unwilling act of giving, and finally envy.
sensesIntro.cn: grudge 从低声抱怨开始，变成长期的怨恨，再指怨恨的缘由、不情愿的给予，最后指嫉妒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone kept in the chest for an old hurt.
core.cn: 核心意象：因旧事而压在胸口的一块石头。

branches.en: The lasting anger is the main noun sense.
branches.cn: 长期怒气是主要名词义项。

branches.en: The cause of dislike is the headless noun sense.
branches.cn: 不满的缘由是较抽象的义项。

branches.en: Giving unwillingly is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 勉强给予是动词义项。

branches.en: A quiet complaint can harden into a held grudge.
branches.cn: 低声抱怨会硬化成怀在心里的怨。

branches.en: Not wanting to give reaches back to envy of others.
branches.cn: 不愿给予可追溯为对别人的嫉妒。

intro.en: Grudge is a French borrowing with an uncertain Germanic source; its English family uses be-, -ing, -ly, and -er.
intro.cn: grudge 是来自法语的借词，其日耳曼来源不确定；英语词族用到 be-、-ing、-ly、-er 等成分。

latinIntro.en: The immediate source is Old French grouchier, probably Germanic, so no Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是古法语 grouchier，一般认为出自日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Grouchier is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: grouchier 是直接来源。

items.example: Grudge keeps the complaint sense.
items.exampleCN: grudge 保留了抱怨的含义。

items.example: The verb grudge takes an object.
items.exampleCN: 动词 grudge 后接宾语。

items.example: Be- makes begrudge.
items.exampleCN: be- 构成 begrudge。

items.example: Begrudge adds envy to the giving.
items.exampleCN: begrudge 给「给予」加上嫉妒。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms grudging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 grudging。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms grudgingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 grudgingly。

items.example: The suffix -er forms grudger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 grudger。

definition_zh: 低声埋怨；发牢骚；嘟囔；发出低鸣
definition_en: to complain in a low, unhappy voice, often quietly and repeatedly
core_image: 垂着头的人，咽喉深处低低地嗡鸣，像在埋怨
scene: 会开得很晚，角落里有人久久埋怨。In the corner of the room, one weary colleague kept grumbling about the endless meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 grumble 是低声埋怨（第1个义项：压低嗓门、屡屡道出憋闷）；角落里有人久久埋怨。

pos.zh: 低声埋怨；发牢骚；嘟囔；发出低鸣

derivatives.zh: 爱发牢骚者：加 -er 造出的施事名号字
嗡鸣渐缓的埋怨：-ing 造出的名称
爱埋怨的：加 -y 造出，偏于口头
气鼓鼓地：脾气类词

senses.title: To complain in a low, unhappy voice
senses.definition: to voice a grievance in a quiet, low voice, usually with a note of sulking
senses.definitionCN: 用压低而闷的嗓道出憋闷，常含闷闷的口吻
senses.example: The staff grumbled about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 职工嫌新时刻表，低声埋怨。
senses.why: The word copies a low rolling murmur, so sense one is a stream of hushed complaints.
senses.whyCN: 此词仿压低的滚动哝声，所以开头就道出埋怨。

senses.title: To make a low rumbling sound
senses.definition: of a belly, a motor or far thunder, to keep giving off a deep rolling noise
senses.definitionCN: 胃肠、马达或遥远的雷霆不停地发出深沉滚动的窸窣声
senses.example: Her hungry belly grumbled right through the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她那空胃肠在考试中途低鸣不停。
senses.why: The deep roll of a sullen voice is lent to an empty belly or a distant motor.
senses.whyCN: 低而闷的话，拿去描摹空胃肠或那台马达。

senses.title: A complaint said quietly
senses.definition: a grievance voiced low by one person or a small crowd, not put forward as open protest
senses.definitionCN: 某人或若干人压低声道出的憋闷
senses.example: There was a low grumble from the back row.
senses.exampleCN: 后排涌起低低的埋怨。
senses.why: As a noun the verb points back at its product, that is the uneasy words just voiced.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，动作的话就是刚说出的话。

senses.title: A dull continuous noise
senses.definition: a deep dull sound kept up by thunder, traffic or a far motor
senses.definitionCN: 由雷霆、车流或远方马达保持着的深沉闷响
senses.example: We heard the grumble of thunder beyond the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见山那边雷声沉沉。
senses.why: The rumbling side of the word grows into a noun for any deep sound that rolls on endlessly.
senses.whyCN: 词里的滚动成了名词，说滚个不停的闷响。

senses.title: To complain out of habit
senses.definition: to keep airing small grievances by force of habit, never hoping to alter anything
senses.definitionCN: 凭习性屡屡道出些闷话
senses.example: He grumbles for a minute, then returns to his work.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘟囔片刻，随后又去做事。
senses.why: Words kept low mark a ritual: a grumble discharges feeling rather than seeking action.
senses.whyCN: 低嗓显出这是礼节：埋怨只吐闷气。

intro.en: The origin of grumble is uncertain; most dictionaries call it echoic, shaped to sound like a low murmur.
intro.cn: grumble 出处未明，多数词典称其属拟声，仿低沉哝声。

items.en: No secure root is known, and the word is widely described as echoic.
items.cn: 字根始终未见，往往称拟声词。

items.en: Low murmur words of similar shape exist in Germanic tongues, yet the exact link stays uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸亲族里有类似的低声词，关联未明。

items.en: Grumble is logged in the sixteenth century as a word for murmuring in protest.
items.cn: 十六世纪英文里涌现 grumble，用于带怨气地哝。

items.en: The sense of a rolling noise, as of a belly or thunder, is added.
items.cn: 十八世纪又添滚动声的涵义，好比肠胃低鸣或雷鸣。

items.en: Modern dictionaries keep the uncertain origin together with the echoic note.
items.cn: 现代词典维持出处未明，并保留拟声注。

note.en: Grumble stands among complaint words such as mutter and whine, and beside rumble words for deep noise.
note.cn: grumble 夹在 mutter、whine 等埋怨词中间，也挨着 rumble 这类深沉的低声词。

entries.definition: bad-tempered and easily annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 脾气坏、易发火

entries.definition: to give off a deep rolling sound
entries.definitionCN: 发出低沉的隆隆响声

entries.definition: a person who complains often
entries.definitionCN: 常发牢骚者

entries.definition: complaints, or a low rolling noise
entries.definitionCN: 埋怨；低低的滚动声

entries.definition: to speak low and unclearly, often with displeasure
entries.definitionCN: 低声含糊地讲，常带不悦

entries.definition: to complain in a high, drawn-out voice
entries.definitionCN: 用又高又拖的声调埋怨

entries.definition: to say that something makes you unhappy
entries.definitionCN: 埋怨、申诉（最普通讲法）

normalIntro.en: Grumble is the sound of a low voice that keeps a complaint alive.
normalIntro.cn: grumble 就是压得很低的那片埋怨。

normal.en: Grumble about is the usual frame for a hushed complaint.
normal.cn: grumble about 是低声埋怨的常用框架。

normal.en: The noun grumble names a complaint kept low, never a loud protest.
normal.cn: 名称字 grumble 表压低的埋怨，绝非高呼。

normal.en: Grumble and rumble share a shape and both name deep noise.
normal.cn: grumble 与 rumble 酷似。

normal.en: Typical frames: grumble that fares rose, or grumble at a child.
normal.cn: 常用框架：grumble that 接埋怨要旨，grumble at 接埋怨谁。

normal.en: A grumbler repeats complaints yet never raises a voice.
normal.cn: grumbler 屡屡埋怨，从不抬高嗓门。

abstract.en: Picture a worker leaning on a counter, talking to himself.
abstract.cn: 设想某劳工靠在柜台旁自说自话。

abstract.en: Bring to mind a long queue where everyone hums low.
abstract.cn: 脑海浮现队列，人人低声哼哝。

abstract.en: Think of a belly that rumbles as a speaker drones on.
abstract.cn: 想见讲者絮叨过后，胃肠低鸣阵阵。

examples.en: Commuters grumbled that the fare had gone up again.
examples.cn: 通勤客埋怨票价又涨了。

examples.en: An old ferry grumbled across the dark harbour.
examples.cn: 旧渡轮在暗沉沉的海港里轰隆着穿行。

examples.en: After the pay cut there was a quiet grumble among staff.
examples.cn: 减薪往后，员工间涌现低声埋怨。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐记 · 咕噜姆，非考据
dict_mnemonic.text: 「咕噜」——嗓门压得低，嗡嗡连声，就是 grumble。只算谐记，绝非考据。

root: 出处未明，通常称拟声词，仿低沉的滚动哝声。

sensesIntro.en: Grumble starts as a hushed complaint, settles into a habit of low griping, and then lends its deep roll to rumbling noises.
sensesIntro.cn: 最初是压低的埋怨，随后成了惯常牢骚，最终把那股深沉滚动借给各类隆隆声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deep voice rolling out a complaint.
core.cn: 核心画面：深沉的嗓滚出埋怨。

branches.en: A hushed complaint is the central verb sense.
branches.cn: 嗓门很低的埋怨就是主要动词义。

branches.en: A belly or a motor grumbles with the same deep roll.
branches.cn: 胃肠与马达都能这样低沉地 grumble。

branches.en: The noun names the complaint just spoken.
branches.cn: 名称字直接表刚讲出的埋怨。

branches.en: Thunder and traffic supply the dull rolling sound.
branches.cn: 雷霆与车流贡献那种沉闷的滚动声。

branches.en: Both a passing complaint and a habitual one are let off rather than argued.
branches.cn: 随口埋怨与惯常牢骚都属释放，并非争辩。

intro.en: Grumble carries no productive English prefix or suffix of its own; its family is narrow and grows from the base stem.
intro.cn: grumble 鲜有能产的英文字头，族很窄。

latinIntro.en: Grumble has no Latin source, so no Latin kinsman is listed.
latinIntro.cn: grumble 在西文里找不着祖词，故不列。

items.meaning: to complain in a low voice
items.example: Grumble is echoic in origin.
items.exampleCN: grumble 出自拟声。

items.example: Grumble also works as a noun.
items.exampleCN: grumble 又作名号字。

items.example: The end -le often marks repeated sounds.
items.exampleCN: -le 使低鸣连绵。

items.example: The suffix -er gives the agent noun.
items.exampleCN: -er 造出施事名称。

items.example: The agent noun is grumbler.
items.exampleCN: 施事名号字是 grumbler。

items.meaning: quiet complaint, or a roll of sound
items.example: The -ing form names the act.
items.exampleCN: -ing 造出名称。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the loose grumbly.
items.exampleCN: -y 造出口头词 grumbly。

items.example: Grumbly is mostly informal.
items.exampleCN: grumbly 偏于口头。

items.example: The phrase grumble about is very common.
items.exampleCN: grumble about 用得极多。

definition_zh: 火药；黑火药；导火索；珠茶；爆发力
definition_en: an early explosive made of saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur, once used to fire guns
core_image: 黑粉沾着火星，轰地炸开成烟
scene: 旧城楼的储物间里，木箱盛着黑粉，旁边倚着锈蚀的火炮。In the storeroom of the old tower, wooden crates held gunpowder beside a rusty cannon.
sceneCN: 此处 gunpowder 即火药（第1个义项：放炮所用的黑粉）；说的是旧城楼储物间里，木箱盛着火药，旁边倚着锈蚀的火炮。

pos.zh: 火药；黑火药；导火索；珠茶；迸发力

derivatives.zh: 细粉；后半出自「poudre」
粉似的；由 -y 示出
研成粉的；由 -ed 示出
火炮；起头出自「gunnr」

senses.title: The black explosive used in firearms
senses.definition: an explosive mixed from saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur, used to fire guns and cannon
senses.definitionCN: 硝石、木炭与硫磺调成的炸药，拿去放枪放炮
senses.example: Early cannon fired balls with gunpowder.
senses.exampleCN: 初时的火炮靠火药把弹丸放出去。
senses.why: The compound joins gun and powder into one name for the powder that fired a gun.
senses.whyCN: 此词把「枪」与「粉」并成名，专说放枪放炮的粉，故起手就称火药。

senses.title: The charge inside a shell or cartridge
senses.definition: the packed powder inside a cartridge, shell or rocket that burns and drives the shot
senses.definitionCN: 装进弹药筒、炮弹或火箭、焚烧后推动弹丸的那份粉
senses.example: Each shell carried a fresh charge of gunpowder.
senses.exampleCN: 炮弹里都装好了新火药。
senses.why: Once the word named the black powder, it could also name the portion loaded inside a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 既然称呼黑粉，也能称呼兵器里装好的粉，于是有弹里所装的火药。

senses.title: A hidden trigger inside a dispute
senses.definition: a thing inside a situation that could set off sudden anger or open conflict
senses.definitionCN: 格局里能点着怒火或公开冲突的某样东西
senses.example: The land claim was pure gunpowder in that debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那项土地主张在辩论里就是火药。
senses.why: Powder works only when it is sparked, so a flashpoint inside a row borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 火药只等火星便炸，争吵里潜着的火花于是借了类似的图画。

senses.title: Green tea rolled into tiny balls
senses.definition: a green tea twisted into tight little pellets, so named because they look like powder grains
senses.definitionCN: 揉成紧密颗粒的绿茶，因像火药颗粒而得名
senses.example: Moroccan tea is made from gunpowder and mint.
senses.exampleCN: 摩洛哥茶用珠茶加薄荷。
senses.why: Grain and balled tea share a look, so the name of the powder was lent to the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 火药颗粒与球状茶叶外貌相仿，于是这名号借给了叶。

senses.title: Rapid burning force in words or writing
senses.definition: fast and forceful energy in speech, prose or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 讲辞、文辞或表演中迅疾而有力的能量
senses.example: Her debut novel is full of emotional gunpowder.
senses.exampleCN: 她处女作的故事里充满爆发力。
senses.why: Powder burns all at once, so vivid and explosive writing is said to hold it.
senses.whyCN: 火药点着便烧尽，故冲击极猛的文辞好比藏着火药。

intro.en: Gunpowder joins gun, borrowed from Old Norse, to powder, drawn from Latin pulvis by way of French.
intro.cn: gunpowder 由 gun 与 powder 相连，gunnr 出自古北欧文，poudre 经古法文通往 pulvis。

items.en: The Latin noun pulvis names dust or fine powder beneath the word powder.
items.cn: powder 底下藏着 pulvis，也就是尘土与细粉。

items.en: The French poudre carries this Latin noun into English as powder.
items.cn: poudre 经古法文通向 pulvis。

items.en: The noun gunnr lies behind English gun, a weapon that fires a shot.
items.cn: gun 出自古北欧文 gunnr，即射出弹丸的兵器。

items.en: The compound gunpowder is settled as the name of the black explosive.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，gunpowder 专门称呼黑粉。

items.en: Modern English adds the tea sense and the fire of vivid prose.
items.cn: 后世又添茶叶个含义与文辞的火。

note.en: Gunpowder belongs beside powder, gun and gunnery, and near words for things that blow up.
note.cn: gunpowder 与「gun」「gunnery」出于 gun，也挨着会炸的字。

entries.definition: fine dry grains
entries.definitionCN: 细干颗粒；粉（此词后半）

entries.definition: a weapon that fires a shot
entries.definitionCN: 发射弹丸的兵器（此词头段）

entries.definition: the use of heavy guns
entries.definitionCN: 重炮射击的法

entries.definition: the firing of a gun
entries.definitionCN: 枪响；放枪

entries.definition: a substance that blows up when ignited
entries.definitionCN: 点着便会炸开的物质

entries.definition: a stronger explosive of later years
entries.definitionCN: 后世更猛的烈性炸药

entries.definition: the moment trouble bursts out
entries.definitionCN: 冲突骤起的临界点

normalIntro.en: Gunpowder is gun plus powder, the dry powder that fired a gun.
normalIntro.cn: gunpowder 即「枪」加「粉」，放枪所用的干粉。

normal.en: The name joins two everyday English words.
normal.cn: 此名由「gun」与「powder」并成。

normal.en: Saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur make the old recipe.
normal.cn: 硝石、木炭、硫磺就成旧时作方。

normal.en: The Gunpowder Plot was a plot to blow up a king.
normal.cn: 火药阴谋案是炸死国王的旧案。

normal.en: Gunpowder tea looks like small dark grains of powder.
normal.cn: 珠茶像暗色的细粉粒。

normal.en: Old weapons are called firearms because the powder was lit in a pan.
normal.cn: 旧时兵器叫火器，因粉在药池点着。

abstract.en: See a heap of black grains and one spark.
abstract.cn: 黑粉沾到火星。

abstract.en: Think of a shell packed tight with powder.
abstract.cn: 炮弹里塞紧粉。

abstract.en: Hear one careless word set a quarrel alight.
abstract.cn: 口角因疏忽燃起。

examples.en: Gunpowder reshaped warfare across the known world.
examples.cn: 火药从此重塑兵事。

examples.en: The cellar was stacked with barrels of gunpowder.
examples.cn: 地窖码满成桶的火药。

examples.en: Trade ships carried gunpowder, silk and tea.
examples.cn: 商船载着火药、丝绸与茶叶。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐记 · 杠炮的，非考据
dict_mnemonic.text: 「杠炮的」——杠着炮、等着用的粉，就是火药 gunpowder；这只是谐记，绝非考据。

root: gun（出自古北欧文 gunnr）与 powder（经古法文 poudre 通往 pulvis，尘土与粉）相连，专称放枪用的粉，即火药。

sensesIntro.en: Gunpowder begins as the black explosive, then marks the charge inside a shell, the spark in a row, the grain of tea, and the fire in prose.
sensesIntro.cn: gunpowder 先说黑粉，再说炮弹里装的火药、争斗里的导火索、茶的颗粒，也说到文辞的火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain of black powder met by one spark.
core.cn: 核心画面：黑粉沾到火星。

branches.en: The black explosive is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 黑粉就是字面含义。

branches.en: A charge inside a shell repeats the powder within a weapon.
branches.cn: 弹里所装的药，把粉挪进了炮膛。

branches.en: A hidden spark in a row is powder moved to a quarrel.
branches.cn: 争吵里潜着的火花，是粉挪进了口角。

branches.en: Balled tea copies the grain of the powder.
branches.cn: 揉成球的叶仿了粉粒的外貌。

branches.en: Raw powder and the fire in prose both burst out fast.
branches.cn: 原样黑粉与文辞的火，都炸得极快。

intro.en: Gunpowder is a compound of two free forms, gun and powder, without prefix or suffix of its own.
intro.cn: gunpowder 里 gun 与 powder 相连，不带字头。

latinIntro.en: The powder part goes back to Latin pulvis, dust, through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 表粉的半边，经古法文通往 pulvis，即尘土。

items.example: Gun is borrowed from Old Norse.
items.exampleCN: gun 出自「古北欧文」。

items.example: Powder comes from French poudre.
items.exampleCN: powder 出自「法文 poudre」。

items.example: The compound names the explosive.
items.exampleCN: 此词就叫黑粉。

items.example: Gun marks the first half.
items.exampleCN: gun 起头。

items.example: Powder marks the second half.
items.exampleCN: powder 是后半。

items.example: The -y form gives powdery.
items.exampleCN: 加 -y 得 powdery。

items.example: The suffix -y forms powdery.
items.exampleCN: -y 造出 powdery。

items.example: The -ed form gives powdered.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ed 得 powdered。

items.example: Gun also forms gunshot.
items.exampleCN: gun 也造出 gunshot。

definition_zh: 涌出；喷涌；滔滔不绝地讲；赞美充溢
definition_en: to flow out suddenly and in large amounts, as from a crack or a pipe
core_image: 水管开缝，水柱带泡直冲
scene: 老水管在深夜爆开，水流涌进走廊，淹了半个厅。An old pipe burst in the night and water gushed into the hall.
sceneCN: 此处 gush 说「涌出」（第1个义项：水流从裂口猛冲而出）；讲的是老水管爆开，水流涌进走廊。

pos.zh: 涌出；喷涌；滔滔不绝地讲

collocations.zh: 涌出……；因某种心绪而激奋

derivatives.zh: 滔滔不绝的；热切过头
矫饰、热切过头
喷油井；感受外露的人
斜切面；苏格兰行话

senses.title: To pour out suddenly in a large flow
senses.definition: of liquid or gas, to rush out fast and in a wide stream from a crack
senses.definitionCN: 水与气从裂口急速成股冲出
senses.example: Water gushed from the cracked pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 水从裂开的水管涌出。
senses.why: The word copies the sound and force of a sudden rush, so the core sense is a wide, bursting flow.
senses.whyCN: 此词仿骤冲的声响，故核心义就是猛地涌出

senses.title: To spill over in a crowd or rush
senses.definition: of people or crowds, to come out quickly in a throng
senses.definitionCN: 人群急速成团涌出
senses.example: Fans gushed through the gates at the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声末响，球迷从门口蜂拥出
senses.why: A sudden flow of water offers a ready picture for a crowd that bursts out at once.
senses.whyCN: 骤然涌出的水流，正好拿去描摹即刻冲出的人群

senses.title: To talk with eager, unbroken excitement
senses.titleCN: 滔滔不绝地讲；热切地说
senses.definition: to speak or write with so much eager feeling that the words keep pouring out
senses.definitionCN: 带着热切的感受不停讲或下笔，话像水似地淌出
senses.example: She gushed about her new job for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她不停夸这工作，讲了快半刻钟
senses.why: Speech that will not stop looks like water that will not stop, so the flow of water becomes a flow of words.
senses.whyCN: 说不完的话好比流不完的水，故水涌也成了话涌

senses.title: A sudden strong flow
senses.definition: a sudden mass of liquid, gas or other matter that comes out in one burst
senses.definitionCN: 水、气或其他东西骤然成股涌出的量
senses.example: A gush of warm air met us at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 开门时暖风迎面
senses.why: The noun names the burst itself, the amount that comes out at a single spurt.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时称喷涌，也就是猛喷出的份量。

senses.title: Words of excessive praise
senses.definition: a show of over-warm praise or feeling that seems to pour out
senses.definitionCN: 热切过头、像水倒出的赞美或心绪
senses.example: The letters were full of gush about the young singer.
senses.exampleCN: 那些信里满是溢美辞，全夸这歌手
senses.why: Since gushing speech is felt to be too much, the noun also names feeling that spills over.
senses.whyCN: 既然滔滔不绝的言辞过头，名词便称夸得过火的心绪。

intro.en: Gush is of uncertain origin, though it is widely treated as echoic, built to sound like water rushing out.
intro.cn: 「出处」未详；通常视作拟声词，仿水猛冲声。

items.en: No secure root is agreed on, and the word is often called echoic.
items.cn: 词根未有结论，往往称作拟声词。

items.en: Gush appears in the sixteenth century as a word for water bursting out.
items.cn: 十六世纪中，gush 称水骤涌。

items.en: The word is also used for a crowd pouring out through an opening.
items.cn: 此词也用于人群从开口处涌出。

items.en: The sense of over-warm talk or writing is added.
items.cn: 十九世纪又添热切过头的言辞。

items.en: Modern dictionaries keep the uncertain origin and the echoic note.
items.cn: 现代词典保留出处不详与拟声的注释。

note.en: Gush belongs with flow words such as pour, spurt and surge, and with the family of gushing and gushy.
note.cn: gush 与「pour」「spurt」「surge」皆属流动类词，又与「gushing」「gushy」结成词族。

entries.definition: pouring out, or over-warm in speech
entries.definitionCN: 涌出的；热切过头的

entries.definition: too warm and effusive
entries.definitionCN: 过于热切做作的

entries.definition: a well that flows by itself
entries.definitionCN: 自喷井；感受外露的人

entries.definition: to wash out with a rush of water
entries.definitionCN: 用水冲洗；脸红（与 gush 相似）

entries.definition: to make liquid flow steadily
entries.definitionCN: 使水不断流出

entries.definition: to come out in a short sharp burst
entries.definitionCN: 急促地喷

entries.definition: to move forward in a heavy wave
entries.definitionCN: 成浪涌着往处

normalIntro.en: Gush is the rush of water that finds a crack and comes out all at once.
normalIntro.cn: gush 就是水找到裂缝后猛地冲出的劲头。

normal.en: Gush out is the plainest pattern for a burst of water.
normal.cn: gush out 是水流冲出的常用「框架」。

normal.en: To gush over a person is to praise that person without pause.
normal.cn: gush over 某人，就是向着「那个人」不歇地夸。

normal.en: A gusher is an oil well that flows up by itself.
normal.cn: gusher 称靠压力涌出的油井。

normal.en: Gushing praise is thought to be excessive, so the word carries a hint of doubt.
normal.cn: 滔滔的赞美显得过头，故此词含些许怀疑。

normal.en: Compare surge and spurt, which also borrow water for force and suddenness.
normal.cn: 比照「surge」与「spurt」，「二者」皆借水讲「力」与骤然。

abstract.en: See a split in a dam and a white jet shooting out.
abstract.cn: 设想堤坝裂开，雪亮的柱直冲。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pouring through one narrow gate.
abstract.cn: 设想人群从「窄门」涌过。

abstract.en: Hear someone praise a singer without stopping for breath.
abstract.cn: 设想某人夸赞歌手，「片刻」不歇。

examples.en: Oil gushed from the well for a whole week.
examples.cn: 油井不停喷了整周。

examples.en: Blood gushed from the wound before the doctor arrived.
examples.cn: 医者未到，血直从伤口涌出。

examples.en: She gushed about the film to everyone she met.
examples.cn: 她见人便滔滔不绝地夸那部电影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「骨嘘」——水管开缝，水骨碌骨碌地冲出，就是 gush；这只是谐记，绝非考据。

root: 「出处」未详；通常视作拟声词，仿水猛冲声。

sensesIntro.en: Gush starts with liquid bursting out, lends itself to crowds pouring through a gate, then becomes a rush of words and a burst of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: gush 从水冲出说起，又借给涌出的人群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack in a pipe and a jet of water.
core.cn: 核心画面：水管裂缝与冲出的水。

branches.en: A sudden wide flow is the core sense.
branches.cn: 骤然成股涌出是核心义。

branches.en: A crowd gushes like water through a gap.
branches.cn: 人群像水似地从「门缝」涌出。

branches.en: Endless speech borrows the endless flow.
branches.cn: 滔滔不绝的话借了不停的水流。

branches.en: The noun names a single burst of that flow.
branches.cn: 名词称那道涌流。

branches.en: Words that pour out too freely turn into over-warm praise.
branches.cn: 倾倒过火，就成了夸。

intro.en: Gush has no productive prefix; its small family is built with English endings.
intro.cn: gush 字族极窄，只靠词干。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is known for gush, so none is listed.
latinIntro.cn: gush 并非出自西文，故不列。

items.example: Gush is echoic in origin.
items.exampleCN: gush 属「拟声」出处。

items.example: Gush also works as a noun.
items.exampleCN: gush 又作名词。

items.example: The -ing form gives gushing.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ing 得 gushing。

items.example: The -y form gives gushy.
items.exampleCN: 加 -y 得 gushy。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The -er form gives gusher.
items.exampleCN: 加 -er 得 gusher。

items.example: Gushing water filled the lane.
items.exampleCN: 涌出的水漫满街巷。

items.example: The card was rather gushy.
items.exampleCN: 那张卡片笔墨有点肉麻。

items.example: The gusher lasted for days.
items.exampleCN: 那口自喷井喷了几天。

definition_zh: 大口喝；狼吞虎咽；大量消耗；猛冲；咕咚一口
definition_en: to drink or eat something fast and greedily, or to swallow up fuel, money, or resources
core_image: 一个干渴的人抱着易拉罐一仰头，把整罐饮料灌进喉咙
scene: 夏日球场的看台边，刚跑完步的人汗流浃背。He guzzled a whole bottle of cold water before the whistle blew.
sceneCN: 这里 guzzle 是「大口喝、猛灌」（第 1 个义项：急切而贪婪地喝）；句意：哨声响起之前，他把一整瓶冰水灌了下去。可想象的画面：栏杆、冰镇的瓶子、仰起的脖子。

pos.zh: 动词：大口喝；狼吞虎咽；大量消耗
名词：一次大口吞咽；咕咚一声

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「豪饮者；耗油大的车」
由本词加 -ing 名词化构成，义为「豪饮；大量消耗」

senses.title: To drink quickly and greedily
senses.definition: to drink something quickly, in large mouthfuls, especially because one is very thirsty
senses.definitionCN: 尤因非常口渴而大口、快速地喝
senses.example: After the marathon he guzzled two bottles of water.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完马拉松后，他两口灌下了两瓶水。
senses.why: The image is a throat that gulps as fast as it can, so the word keeps the big, noisy swallow at its centre.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一个拼命吞咽的喉咙，所以这个词始终保留着大口、带声的吞咽动作。

senses.title: To eat rapidly
senses.definition: to eat food rapidly, especially food that is junk food or eaten in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 快速大量地吃，尤其指吃垃圾食品
senses.example: The teenagers guzzled chips and chocolate all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那些青少年整个下午都在猛吃薯片和巧克力。
senses.why: Once the greedy swallow is established, it easily moves from drink to food, keeping the same speed and lack of restraint.
senses.whyCN: 贪婪吞咽的画面一旦确立，就很容易从「喝」转到「吃」，速度与毫无节制的感觉保持不变。

senses.title: To consume resources
senses.definition: to use up a large amount of fuel, money, or energy in a wasteful way
senses.definitionCN: 以浪费的方式大量消耗燃料、金钱或精力
senses.example: Old trucks guzzle fuel and money.
senses.exampleCN: 老旧卡车既费油又费钱。
senses.why: A machine that swallows fuel is pictured like a thirsty throat, so fuel consumption borrows the verb directly.
senses.whyCN: 把吞油如吞水的机器想象成一张干渴的喉咙，于是燃料消耗直接借用了这个动词。

senses.title: A lurching movement
senses.definition: to move or or make a rushing, lurching motion, as in a sudden rush of liquid or flame
senses.definitionCN: 猛地冲一下或颠动，如液体、火焰猛然涌出
senses.example: A blue flame guzzled up through the grate.
senses.exampleCN: 一团蓝色的火苗从炉栅间猛地窜起。
senses.why: English already had guzzle for a surging rush of flame or liquid; the greedy swallow sits inside this rushing sense.
senses.whyCN: 英语早就有 guzzle 表示火苗或液体猛冲的用法，它「猛然吞咽」的意象正藏在这股猛冲里。

senses.title: A noisy drinking pause
senses.definition: a short pause in speech for a noisy gulp of drink, or the gulp itself
senses.definitionCN: 说话间停下来灌一口水的短暂停顿，或那一声咕咚
senses.example: He paused for a guzzle of tea and went on.
senses.exampleCN: 他停下来灌了一口茶，又继续说下去。
senses.why: The name of the action becomes a name for the thing: one swallow of drink can be called a guzzle.
senses.whyCN: 动作的名称也会变成事物的名称：一次灌下的一口饮料也可以叫一个 guzzle。

intro.en: Guzzle is first recorded in the late sixteenth century; it probably imitates the sound and motion of a throat gulping, and its deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: guzzle 最早见于十六世纪后期，一般认为它模仿喉咙吞咽的声音与动作，更深层的词源「来源不确定」。

items.en: Usually explained as an imitative word for a wet, noisy gulp; the older root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为它是模拟湿润响亮吞咽动作的拟声词，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Guzzle means to swallow greedily, mostly of drink.
items.cn: 英语 guzzle 指贪婪地吞咽，多用于饮酒。

items.en: The noun guzzle, one deep draught, becomes common.
items.cn: 名词 guzzle 表示「一大口」，开始常见。

items.en: The word extends to flames and engines that swallow fuel.
items.cn: 词义扩展到吞噬一切的火焰与耗油的机器。

items.en: Guzzler and gas-guzzler keep the greedy-swallow image alive.
items.cn: guzzler 与 gas-guzzler 让「贪婪吞咽」的意象延续至今。

note.en: Guzzle shares the greedy-swallow image with gulp and swig, and sits close to devour, whereas sip names the opposite pace.
note.cn: guzzle 与 gulp、swig 共享「大口吞咽」的意象，与 devour 近义，而 sip 表示相反的小口慢饮。

entries.definition: a greedy drinker, or a car that burns fuel fast
entries.definitionCN: 豪饮者；耗油大的车（与 guzzle 同根）

entries.definition: the feeling of having done wrong
entries.definitionCN: 内疚；罪行（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a stringed musical instrument
entries.definitionCN: 吉他（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自希腊语）

entries.definition: to swallow quickly in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大口吞咽；猛灌

entries.definition: to drink in long gulps
entries.definitionCN: 痛饮；大口喝

entries.definition: to eat food very quickly and hungrily
entries.definitionCN: 狼吞虎咽；吞噬

normalIntro.en: Guzzle is the sound and speed of a throat gulping: remember the -zz- as the rush of liquid going down.
normalIntro.cn: guzzle 就是喉咙吞咽的声音与速度：记住中间的 -zz-，那是液体直往下灌的急流声。

normal.en: Guzzle down a drink means to finish it in seconds.
normal.cn: guzzle down a drink 指几秒钟内把饮料喝完。

normal.en: Guzzle fuel describes a car that drinks petrol fast.
normal.cn: guzzle fuel 形容耗油很快的车。

normal.en: A guzzler is someone or something that gulps things down.
normal.cn: guzzler 指豪饮的人，或大量耗油的机器。

normal.en: Compare gulp, which can be one swallow, with guzzle, which is repeated and greedy.
normal.cn: 对比 gulp：gulp 可以只是一口，guzzle 则是反复而贪婪地灌。

normal.en: The -zz- between two u vowels looks like a throat working fast.
normal.cn: 两个 u 元音之间的 -zz- 像一条正在飞快工作的喉咙。

abstract.en: Picture a runner tipping a bottle straight up and drinking in three seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者在三秒内仰头把整瓶水灌完。

abstract.en: See a teenager swallowing chips without chewing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个少年嚼都不嚼就把薯片吞下去。

abstract.en: Imagine an old truck with a fuel gauge dropping like a waterfall.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆老卡车，油表像瀑布一样往下掉。

examples.en: He guzzled his coffee and dashed for the bus.
examples.cn: 他一口灌下咖啡，冲出去赶公交。

examples.en: The engine guzzles fuel on steep hills.
examples.cn: 这辆车的发动机在陡坡上特别费油。

examples.en: The children guzzled lemonade after the football match.
examples.cn: 足球赛结束后，孩子们把柠檬水一饮而尽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尬滋乐」——喝水喝得咕嘟咕嘟滋作响，乐在其中；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: guzzle 来源不确定，一般认为模仿喉咙吞咽的声音与动作（拟声），由「大口吞咽」发展出「狼吞虎咽」「大量消耗燃料、金钱」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Guzzle starts from a greedy swallow of drink and then widens to eating, to burning fuel, and even to a sudden rush.
sensesIntro.cn: guzzle 从「贪婪地喝」出发，依次扩展到吃、消耗燃料，最后还能表示猛然冲涌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thirsty throat tipping back a whole bottle.
core.cn: 核心意象：干渴的喉咙仰头灌下一整瓶。

branches.en: Fast greedy drinking is the original everyday sense.
branches.cn: 快速贪婪地喝是最基本的日常义项。

branches.en: Drink and food share the same speed and the same lack of restraint.
branches.cn: 喝与吃共享同样的速度与毫无节制。

branches.en: A thirsty machine swallowing fuel copies a thirsty person swallowing water.
branches.cn: 渴油的机器吞噬燃料，正是渴水的人吞咽水的翻版。

branches.en: A surge of flame or liquid keeps the rushing motion of a gulp.
branches.cn: 火焰或液体的猛涌保留了吞咽的冲劲。

branches.en: The noun names a lurching movement as well as a single noisy swallow.
branches.cn: 名词形式既指一次咕咚吞咽，也指猛然的一冲。

intro.en: Guzzle is a simple imitative verb with little affixation; its family grows with -er and -ing.
intro.cn: guzzle 是一个拟声式的简单动词，附加成分很少，词族主要靠 -er 与 -ing 生长。

latinIntro.en: Guzzle has no Latin word behind it, so the Latin entries are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: guzzle 背后没有拉丁语来源，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Guzzle is the base form of the family.
items.exampleCN: guzzle 是这一词族的基础形式。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.meaningCN: 表示做事的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms guzzler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 guzzler。

items.meaning: a greedy drinker or a fuel-hungry vehicle
items.example: A guzzler drinks or burns too fast.
items.exampleCN: guzzler 指喝得太快或烧油太猛的东西。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun guzzling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 guzzling。

items.meaningCN: 表示「彻底、完」的副词小品词
items.example: Guzzle down adds the idea of finishing.
items.exampleCN: guzzle down 补上「喝光」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表示向上、用尽的副词小品词
items.example: Guzzle up describes flames swallowing things.
items.exampleCN: guzzle up 描述火焰吞没东西。

items.example: The compound gas-guzzler means a thirsty car.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 gas-guzzler 指非常耗油的车。

items.meaning: a vehicle that uses too much fuel
items.example: Gas-guzzler puts fuel and the greedy drinker together.
items.exampleCN: gas-guzzler 把燃料与贪婪的饮者合在一起。

definition_zh: 可居住的；适合居住的；宜居的；可入住的
definition_en: suitable or good enough for people to live in, and by extension able to support life
core_image: 一间收拾好的屋子，灯亮着、窗户开着，人可以放心住进去
scene: 地震过后，村里许多土墙房子都裂了缝，只有山顶那间小屋还完好。The mountain hut remained habitable through the whole winter.
sceneCN: 这里 habitable 是「适合居住的、可以住人」（第 1 个义项：房屋适合居住）；句意：那间山中小屋整个冬天都可以住人。可想象的画面：没有裂缝的土墙、亮着灯的窗、冒着烟的烟囱。

pos.zh: 形容词：可居住的；适合居住的；宜居的

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不可居住的」，与 habitable 相反
由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「宜居性；可居住性」
与 habitare 同源，义为「居住于；栖居于」
inhabit 加 -ant 构成，义为「居民；栖息动物」
拉丁语 habitare 的直系名词，义为「栖息地」

senses.title: Suitable for people to live in
senses.definition: fit or good enough for people to live in comfortably, usually of a house or room
senses.definitionCN: 房屋或房间适合让人舒适地居住
senses.example: After the repairs, the flat was habitable again.
senses.exampleCN: 修好之后，这套公寓又可以住人了。
senses.why: The root habitare means to dwell, so a place that can be dwelt in is literally a place that can be inhabited.
senses.whyCN: 词根 habitare 意为「居住」，所以一个能被居住的地方，字面上就是可以住的地方。

senses.title: Fit for life, not merely survival
senses.definition: offering decent, healthy conditions for living rather than bare survival
senses.definitionCN: 提供体面、健康的生活条件，而不只是勉强活着
senses.example: Sunlight and fresh air made the attic habitable.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光和新鲜空气让阁楼变得宜居。
senses.why: From a bare minimum of shelter, the word stretches toward comfortable conditions, from can be lived in to worth living in.
senses.whyCN: 从遮风挡雨的最低限度出发，这个词延伸到舒适的条件，从「能住」变成「值得住」。

senses.title: Suited to life on a planet
senses.titleCN: 可居住的；适合生命存在的
senses.definition: having conditions such as water and mild temperature in which life could survive, usually of a planet or region
senses.definitionCN: 行星或地区具备水、适宜温度等可让生命存续的条件
senses.example: Astronomers found a habitable planet around a nearby star.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家在一颗邻近的恒星旁发现了一颗宜居行星。
senses.why: Astronomy borrowed the word from housing: if people could live on a world, that world is habitable.
senses.whyCN: 天文学借用住房的词汇：如果人类能在某个星球上生活，这个星球就是可居住的。

senses.title: Restored to a usable state
senses.titleCN: 修到能住的样子；恢复可用
senses.definition: made clean, safe, and usable again after damage or neglect
senses.definitionCN: 在损坏或荒废之后被清理、修整得安全可用
senses.example: Builders worked all week to make the cottage habitable.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们干了一整周，才把小屋修到能住人。
senses.why: If a place cannot be dwelt in, the repair work is judged by whether it becomes habitable again.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个地方无法居住，修整工作的成败就看它是否重新变得可以住人。

senses.title: Able to be occupied
senses.definition: legally ready for people to move into, as in a rental property or a building control sense
senses.definitionCN: 指房屋在法律或验收意义上已可让人入住
senses.example: The landlord must issue a habitable certificate before letting.
senses.exampleCN: 房东出租前必须出具一份可入住证明。
senses.why: When renting, the word turns a physical condition into a legal standard that the property must meet.
senses.whyCN: 在租房场景中，这个词把物理条件变成了房屋必须满足的法律标准。

intro.en: Habitable comes from Latin habitabilis, able to be dwelt in, from habitare, to dwell, which is tied to the verb meaning to have or hold.
intro.cn: habitable 来自拉丁语 habitabilis（可居住的），源于 habitare（居住），与表示「持有、占据」的动词有关。

items.en: Habitare means to dwell, and habitabilis means fit to be dwelt in.
items.cn: habitare 意为居住，habitabilis 意为适合居住。

items.en: Roman writers already use habitabilis of land where people can live.
items.cn: 罗马作家已用 habitabilis 形容有人居住的土地。

items.en: The root -bilis means able to be, giving the suffix -able in English.
items.cn: 词根 -bilis 意为「可以被……的」，在英语中变成后缀 -able。

items.en: English borrows habitable chiefly in descriptions of distant lands.
items.cn: 英语借入 habitable，最初多用于描述遥远的地方。

items.en: Modern English uses habitable for housing, building control, and for planets.
items.cn: 现代英语用它形容住房、建筑验收，乃至其他行星。

note.en: Habitable belongs to the habit-dwelling family and pairs with habitat and inhabit, while liveable and habitation stand nearest in meaning.
note.cn: habitable 属于「居住」词族，与 habitat、inhabit 同根，意义最近的是 livable 与 habitation。

entries.definition: the natural home of a plant or animal
entries.definitionCN: 动植物天然的栖息地；与 habitable 同根

entries.definition: to live in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住于；栖居于；与 habitable 同根

entries.definition: a routine behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 习惯（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 habere 的「状态、衣着」义）

entries.definition: pleasant and suitable to live in
entries.definitionCN: 宜居住的；适合生活的

entries.definition: the act of living in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住；聚居地；与 habitable 同根

entries.definition: too damaged to live in
entries.definitionCN: 不适于居住的；无法住人的

normalIntro.en: Habitable is habit plus -able: a place can host the habit of living, so it is a place where a dwelling can continue.
normalIntro.cn: habitable 就是 habit 加 -able：一个地方能容纳「居住」这件事，就是可以持续住下去的地方。

normal.en: Habitable zone names the band of orbits where water stays liquid.
normal.cn: habitable zone 指水能保持液态的行星轨道区域，即宜居带。

normal.en: Inhabitable adds in- and flips the sense to not fit to live in.
normal.cn: inhabitable 加上否定前缀 in-，意义翻转为「不可居住的」。

normal.en: Habitat is the related noun for where a creature lives.
normal.cn: habitat 是同根名词，指生物的栖息地。

normal.en: Habitability is the quality of being fit to live in.
normal.cn: habitability 是「宜居性」这个抽象名词。

normal.en: Compare livable: both mean fit to live in, while habitable sounds more official and scientific.
normal.cn: 对比 livable：两者都表示宜居，habitable 更正式、更科学。

abstract.en: Picture a house with a light in the window and smoke from the chimney.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋窗里亮着灯、烟囱冒着烟的屋子。

abstract.en: See a checklist ticking clean water, fresh air, and a firm roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一张打勾的清单：干净的水、新鲜的空气、结实的屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a green dot on a space map where a ship could land and stay.
abstract.cn: 想象太空地图上一个绿点，飞船可以降落并长住。

examples.en: Parts of the desert are barely habitable.
examples.cn: 那片沙漠的部分地区几乎无法住人。

examples.en: Scientists search for habitable worlds beyond our solar system.
examples.cn: 科学家在太阳系之外寻找宜居世界。

examples.en: Clean water and a warm room made the shelter habitable.
examples.cn: 干净的水和温暖的房间让这个避难所变得可以居住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「还必特保」——一个能住人的地方，还必定要特别注意保暖；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 habitare（居住）+ -abilis（可……的）→ habitabilis → 古法语 habitable → 英语 habitable，核心义「住得下去的」。

sensesIntro.en: Habitable starts from a flat or house one can live in, widens to comfortable living, and then reaches other planets and rented property.
sensesIntro.cn: habitable 从能住人的房子出发，扩展到舒适居住，再延伸到行星宜居与房屋可入住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with a light on, ready for someone to move in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着灯，随时可以搬进去的屋子。

branches.en: A house fit to live in is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 可以住人的房子是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Comfortable living takes the basic sense one step further.
branches.cn: 舒适居住把基本义项向前推了一步。

branches.en: Planets borrow the word by replacing people with life.
branches.cn: 行星借用这个词，只是把「人」换成「生命」。

branches.en: Repair work is measured by how habitable it leaves a place.
branches.cn: 修整工作看的是修完能不能住人。

branches.en: Restoring a dwelling and legal readiness to occupy both point back to the same image.
branches.cn: 修好住处与通过验收可入住，都回指同一个意象。

intro.en: Habitable is built from the Latin root habit- plus the suffix -able, and it shares this habit- shape with habitat and inhabit.
intro.cn: habitable 由拉丁词根 habit- 加后缀 -able 构成，并与 habitat、inhabit 共享 habit- 这一词形。

latinIntro.en: Latin habitare means to dwell, habitabilis means fit to dwell in, and the suffix -abilis means able to be.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habitare 意为居住，habitabilis 意为适合居住，后缀 -abilis 意为「可被……的」。

items.example: The root habit- carries the idea of living in a place.
items.exampleCN: 词根 habit- 承载「住在某处」的概念。

items.example: The suffix -able turns dwelling into being fit to dwell in.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把「居住」变成「可供居住」。

items.example: Habitable joins the root and the suffix.
items.exampleCN: habitable 把词根与后缀合在一起。

items.example: The prefix in- gives inhabitable its opposite force.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 使 inhabitable 带上了否定的意味。

items.example: Inhabitable reverses the sense of habitable.
items.exampleCN: inhabitable 把 habitable 的意义反转。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms habitability.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 habitability。

items.example: Habitat keeps the old Latin noun meaning home.
items.exampleCN: habitat 保留了拉丁名词「家」的含义。

items.example: Inhabit uses the same root as a verb.
items.exampleCN: inhabit 用同一个词根作动词。

items.example: The suffix -ant names the person who dwells.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 指出居住的人。

definition_zh: 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老套的；因用滥而掉价的
definition_en: used far too often, and therefore no longer fresh, striking, or meaningful
core_image: 一匹被无数人骑过的出租马，走的路和蹄声都成了老套
scene: 演讲比赛前，许多选手都写了「向着梦想奔跑」这样的开场白。Every essay said the same thing in the same hackneyed words.
sceneCN: 这里 hackneyed 是「陈词滥调的、被用滥了的」（第 1 个义项：因重复使用而失去力量）；句意：每篇文章都用同样老套的措辞说着同样的话。可想象的画面：一叠几乎一模一样的稿纸。

pos.zh: 形容词：陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老套的

derivatives.zh: 本词的名词原形，义为「出租马」，再引申为「出租车辆」
与 hackney 同源的短形式，义为「出租马；雇佣文人」，今常指「写手；黑客」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「陈腐；俗套」

senses.title: Overused and no longer effective
senses.definition: repeated so often that it has lost its force, freshness, or meaning
senses.definitionCN: 被反复使用以致失去力量、新鲜感或意义
senses.example: The essay was packed with hackneyed ideas about love.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章塞满了关于爱情的陈词。
senses.why: The core image is a hired horse worn out from carrying too many riders, so anything used this often loses its edge.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一匹被太多骑手用旧了的出租马，任何东西被这么反复使用，就会失去锋芒。

senses.title: A phrase worn out by repetition
senses.definition: describing a word or phrase that has been used so much that it sounds stale
senses.definitionCN: 形容被用得太多、听起来已陈旧乏味的词语
senses.example: The headline used a hackneyed phrase about a city that never sleeps.
senses.exampleCN: 这则标题用了一句关于不夜城的陈词滥调。
senses.why: Phrases are borrowed the way horses were hired, so a hackneyed phrase is one hired out far too many times.
senses.whyCN: 词语就像出租的马一样被反复借出来使用，所以陈腐的语句就是被租用太多次的那一类。

senses.title: Made too familiar to feel new
senses.definition: so familiar through constant repetition that it is no longer striking, as in plots or designs
senses.definitionCN: 因反复出现而变得毫无新意，尤指情节或设计
senses.example: The film ended with the hackneyed twist of a dream.
senses.exampleCN: 电影以「原来是一场梦」的烂俗反转收尾。
senses.why: The worn-out image stretches from phrases to whole stories, since plots are also borrowed and ridden hard.
senses.whyCN: 被用旧的意象从词句扩展到整个故事，因为情节同样是被反复借用的。

senses.title: Cheapened by ordinary use
senses.definition: devalued by being used too often, especially of images or symbols
senses.definitionCN: 因使用过频而贬值，尤指图像或象征
senses.example: The hackneyed image of a dove stands for peace everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 那只被用滥了的鸽子图像到处都代表和平。
senses.why: The horse could be hired by anyone, so ubiquity turns into a kind of cheapness.
senses.whyCN: 这匹马谁都能租，于是「人人都在用」就变成了一种廉价感。

senses.title: Tired and mechanical
senses.definition: showing signs of tired repetition, as if produced automatically rather than thought through
senses.definitionCN: 显出疲于重复的痕迹，像是自动复制而非用心思考
senses.example: His speech was a hackneyed tour of every famous quote.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲把名言挨个走了一遍，活像流水线产品。
senses.why: A hired horse that knows the route walks it without thinking, so a hackneyed performance runs on automatic.
senses.whyCN: 走过无数遍的出租马会不假思索地走老路，所以陈腐的表达也是自动运转的。

intro.en: Hackneyed comes from hackney, an ordinary horse kept for hire, a word first recorded in English around the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: hackneyed 来自 hackney，指供出租的普通马匹，这个词约在十四世纪开始见于英语。

items.en: Hackney names an ordinary riding horse, often one kept for hire.
items.cn: 中古英语 hackney 指普通的乘骑马，多为出租用。

items.en: Hackney horse is a common expression, and hack extends the word to a hired writer.
items.cn: hackney horse 成为常用说法，hack 又把这个词扩展到「雇佣文人」。

items.en: Hackneyed grows out of hackney as worn out by constant use.
items.cn: hackneyed 由 hackney 派生，在十七世纪开始出现。

items.en: Hackneyed meaning overused and stale, applied to words and ideas, is established.
items.cn: hackneyed 表示「用滥而陈腐」的意思，主要用于词语和观念。

items.en: The word covers phrases, plots, and images, while hack survives in a new sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中它覆盖措辞、情节与图像，而 hack 又以新的意义继续使用。

items.en: Hack adds the new sense of writing computer code, or of breaking into systems.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，hack 又发展出编写计算机代码与入侵系统的新意义。

note.en: Hackneyed belongs to the hackney word family and shares its stale meaning with banal, trite, and cliched.
note.cn: hackneyed 属于 hackney 词族，与 banal、trite、cliched 共享「陈腐」意义。

entries.definition: an ordinary horse kept for hire
entries.definitionCN: 出租马；普通马匹

entries.definition: a hired horse or a writer for hire
entries.definitionCN: 出租马；雇佣文人（与 hackney 同源）

entries.definition: a London taxi named after the horses once hired there
entries.definitionCN: 伦敦的出租车，得名于当年出租的马匹（与 hackney 同源）

entries.definition: boring because it lacks originality
entries.definitionCN: 乏味的；没新意的

entries.definition: overused and therefore without force
entries.definitionCN: 陈腐的；用滥的

entries.definition: too predictable because it is used everywhere
entries.definitionCN: 老套的；陈词滥调的

normalIntro.en: Hackneyed is the horse you could hire on any corner: when everyone has ridden the same phrase, it becomes hackneyed.
normalIntro.cn: hackneyed 就是街角随处可见的出租马：一句措辞被所有人都骑过一遍，就变得陈腐了。

normal.en: Hackney began as a hired horse, so the word keeps a sense of overuse.
normal.cn: hackney 原本指出租马，所以这个词始终带着「用得太频繁」的意味。

normal.en: A hackneyed phrase is a phrase ridden by everyone.
normal.cn: hackneyed phrase 就是被人人都骑过一遍的措辞。

normal.en: Hack survives for a writer hired by the piece.
normal.cn: hack 至今仍指按篇取酬的雇佣写手。

normal.en: The noun hackney also names a London taxi in hackney cab.
normal.cn: 名词 hackney 在 hackney cab 里也指伦敦出租车。

normal.en: Compare trite and banal: the same stale idea, but hackneyed carries a picture of a tired horse.
normal.cn: 对比 trite 与 banal：都是陈旧的意思，但 hackneyed 多了一匹疲惫老马的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a tired horse pulling the same cart round the same square.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹疲惫的马拉着同样的车，绕着同样的广场转圈。

abstract.en: See a stack of identical greeting cards with the same lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠一模一样的贺卡，上面写着同样的话。

abstract.en: Hear a phrase repeated until it sounds like an empty echo.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被反复念到听起来只剩空洞的回声。

examples.en: A hackneyed ending ruins an otherwise good novel.
examples.cn: 一个俗套的结尾毁了一本本来不错的小说。

examples.en: Avoid hackneyed expressions in your exam essay.
examples.cn: 考试作文里要避免陈词滥调。

examples.en: The slogan was too hackneyed to impress anyone.
examples.cn: 这个标语太过老套，打动不了任何人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hack 你」——被人反复借用、用旧了的东西就像被 hack 过，变得陈旧；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 hackney（供出租的普通马匹，一般认为与伦敦地名 Hackney 有关的说法较晚且不确定）+ -ed → hackneyed（被用旧的）→「陈腐的」。

sensesIntro.en: Hackneyed grows out of the image of an overworked hired horse and then spreads from phrases to plots, images, and performances.
sensesIntro.cn: hackneyed 出自被骑旧的出租马这一意象，随后从词语扩展到情节、图像与表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tired hired horse that everyone rides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹人人骑过、疲惫的出租马。

branches.en: Overuse removes force, the core sense.
branches.cn: 过度使用去掉力量，这是核心义项。

branches.en: Phrases are the first and most common target.
branches.cn: 词语是最早也最常见的对象。

branches.en: Stories and designs are borrowed and ridden hard as well.
branches.cn: 故事与设计同样被反复借用与使用。

branches.en: Being hired by anyone turns ubiquity into cheapness.
branches.cn: 谁都能租用，使「无处不在」变成了廉价。

branches.en: Cheap images and automatic performances both come from the overworked horse.
branches.cn: 廉价的图像与机械化的表演，都源自那匹被用累的马。

intro.en: Hackneyed is hackney plus -ed, and its family grows with hack, hackney cab, and hackneyedness.
intro.cn: hackneyed 由 hackney 加 -ed 构成，词族里有 hack、hackney cab 与 hackneyedness。

latinIntro.en: Hackney has no Latin origin, so the Latin entries stay empty; it can be split into hack plus -ney.
latinIntro.cn: hackney 没有拉丁语来源，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空；这个词可拆成词干 hack 与词尾 -ney。

items.example: Hackney is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: hackney 是这一词族的基础名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「具有……特征」的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms hackneyed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 hackneyed。

items.meaning: a hired horse, later a writer for hire
items.example: Hack is the short form of hackney horse.
items.exampleCN: hack 是 hackney horse 的短形式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms hackneyedness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 hackneyedness。

items.example: Hackney cab keeps the old hire idea.
items.exampleCN: hackney cab 保留了「出租」的老意思。

items.example: Coach belongs to the same world of hired horses.
items.exampleCN: coach 属于同一个「出租马匹」的词汇世界。

items.example: Hackney horse is the full old phrase.
items.exampleCN: hackney horse 是过去的完整说法。

items.example: Worn and hackneyed both point to use that went too far.
items.exampleCN: worn 与 hackneyed 都指向使用了过久。

definition_zh: 大出血；体内失血；大量流失；巨额亏损
definition_en: a heavy loss of blood from a broken vessel, or a rapid and damaging loss of something valuable
core_image: 水管裂开一道口子，鲜红的水止不住地往外淌
scene: 车祸之后，伤者的腿伤口很深，鲜血不断淌到地上。The paramedics pressed hard to stop the haemorrhage before the ambulance arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 haemorrhage 是「大出血」（第 1 个义项：血管破裂后血液大量流出）；句意：救护人员用力按压止住大出血，直到救护车赶来。

pos.zh: （资金、人才等的）大量流失；巨额亏损
大量出血；（资源）迅速流失

collocations.zh: 大量烧钱；亏钱亏得厉害

derivatives.zh: 由 haemorrhage 去 -e 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「出血的；出血性的」
由 haemorrhage 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「大量失血；持续流失」

senses.title: A heavy flow of blood from a broken vessel
senses.titleCN: 大出血；血管破裂大量失血
senses.definition: a serious loss of blood from a damaged blood vessel, often inside the body or from a wound
senses.definitionCN: 血管受损后大量失血，通常是伤口出血或体内出血
senses.example: The patient died from a massive haemorrhage after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 患者在车祸后因大出血死亡。
senses.why: Greek haima means blood and rhegnynai means to burst forth, so the word pictures blood breaking out of a vessel and pouring out unchecked.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 haima 意为「血」，rhegnynai 意为「迸裂而出」，所以这个词的画面是血破口而出、止不住地流。

senses.title: Stopping the bleeding as a medical act
senses.definition: the medical management of severe bleeding, especially the means used to stop blood loss
senses.definitionCN: 对严重出血的医疗处理，尤指用来止住失血的手段
senses.example: Surgeons worked all night to control the haemorrhage.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生通宵工作以控制出血。
senses.why: Once people began treating blood loss, the noun also named the act of arresting it: the gush becomes something a doctor must stop.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始处理失血问题后，这个名词也用来指「止住」这一行为：喷涌的血变成医生必须控制的对象。

senses.title: A rapid loss of money or resources
senses.definition: a quick and serious drain of money, jobs, members, or other valuables
senses.definitionCN: 金钱、工作岗位、成员或其他宝贵资源的迅速而严重的流失
senses.example: The firm suffered a cash haemorrhage last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年冬天出现了严重的现金流失。
senses.why: A body that loses blood weakens, so a company or institution that loses cash or people is imagined as bleeding the same way.
senses.whyCN: 失血的身体会虚弱，所以失去资金或人员的公司机构也被想象成以同样的方式「流血」。

senses.title: A loss of valued things or people
senses.definition: a large and steady loss of talented people, supporters, or prized things, often to rivals
senses.definitionCN: 有才华的人、支持者或珍贵资源不断大量流失，常流向竞争对手
senses.example: The department survived a haemorrhage of senior researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门挺过了资深研究员的大量流失。
senses.why: When wealth or people are compared to blood, their going away takes on the same urgency: the loss itself is treated as physical.
senses.whyCN: 当财富或人被比作血液时，它们的离去就带上了同样的紧迫感：流失被当作身体层面的损伤。

senses.title: To bleed heavily
senses.definition: to lose a large amount of blood quickly, as from an injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 因受伤或疾病而迅速失去大量血液
senses.example: He was haemorrhaging badly by the time the doctor arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 医生赶到时，他正在大量出血。
senses.why: From the sixteenth century the same root supplied a verb, so the noun became an ongoing action: the bleeding itself.
senses.whyCN: 从十六世纪起，同一词根又衍生出动词，名词于是变成一种持续进行的过程：流血这件事本身。

senses.title: To lose money or members fast
senses.definition: to lose money, customers, or staff very quickly and in harmful amounts
senses.definitionCN: 以有害的速度迅速失去资金、顾客或员工
senses.example: The airline haemorrhaged cash for three straight years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司连续三年大量亏损。
senses.why: If losing blood can be done by the body, losing money can be done by a company; the verb carries the helpless, unstoppable feel of real bleeding.
senses.whyCN: 若身体会流血，公司便也会「流钱」；动词保留了真实流血那种止不住的无力感。

senses.title: A sign of damage in figurative speech
senses.definition: used for any obvious and dangerous leak of value or strength that signals deeper damage
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何明显而危险的资源或实力流失，预示着更深层的损害
senses.example: The leaking budget was a haemorrhage the council could not ignore.
senses.exampleCN: 那个漏钱的预算是一处市政会无法忽视的「大失血」。
senses.why: Because bleeding is a sign of a wound, the word is often used metaphorically to point at hidden damage rather than the loss alone.
senses.whyCN: 因为流血是伤口的信号，这个词常被比喻性地用来指向隐藏的损伤，而不只是流失本身。

intro.en: Haemorrhage comes from Greek haima, blood, and rhegnynai, to burst, through later medical Latin and French.
intro.cn: haemorrhage 源自希腊语 haima（血）与 rhegnynai（迸裂），经后世医学拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Haima means blood and rhegnynai means to break or burst.
items.cn: haima 意为血，rhegnynai 意为破裂、迸出。

items.en: Haimorragia names a bursting out of blood in medical writing.
items.cn: 希腊医学著作中 haimorragia 指血的迸流。

items.en: Latin adopts haemorrhagia as a technical term for a flow of blood.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 haemorrhagia，作为指血液流出的医学术语。

items.en: French hemorrhage carries the medical word further west.
items.cn: 法语 hemorrhage 把这个医学词再向西传播。

items.en: English takes the word as haemorrhage, spelled with ae in British style.
items.cn: 英语以 haemorrhage 的词形借入，英式拼写保留 ae。

items.en: The word spreads to finance and journalism as a metaphor for loss.
items.cn: 这个词扩展至金融与新闻写作，成为「流失」的比喻。

note.en: Haemorrhage belongs to the Greek blood-and-burst family, with its twin spelling hemorrhage and near neighbours such as bleeding and blood loss.
note.cn: haemorrhage 属于希腊语「血与迸裂」这一词族，与美式孪生拼写 hemorrhage 以及 bleeding、blood loss 等邻近概念相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的美式拼写

entries.definition: relating to or caused by bleeding
entries.definitionCN: 出血的；出血性的

entries.definition: a swollen vein near the anus that may bleed
entries.definitionCN: 痔：肛门附近会出血的肿静脉

entries.definition: the loss of blood from the body
entries.definitionCN: 流血；出血

entries.definition: the amount of blood lost, often in medical reports
entries.definitionCN: 失血量

entries.definition: to use up money or energy slowly
entries.definitionCN: 消耗；逐渐耗光（资金或精力）

normalIntro.en: Haemorrhage is Greek haima, blood, joined to a verb meaning to burst, so it always means blood (or value) breaking loose.
normalIntro.cn: haemorrhage 由希腊语 haima（血）加上意为「迸裂」的动词构成，因此始终表示血（或价值）冲破口子外流。

normal.en: The root haemo- means blood and appears in haemoglobin too.
normal.cn: 词根 haemo- 意为血，也出现在 haemoglobin 里。

normal.en: The ending -rrhage means a breaking or bursting out.
normal.cn: 词尾 -rrhage 表示破裂、迸出。

normal.en: British spelling keeps ae; American spelling drops it to hemorrhage.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 ae，美式拼写简化为 hemorrhage。

normal.en: In medical reports, haemorrhage is the formal word for a heavy bleed.
normal.cn: 在医学报告中，haemorrhage 是大出血的正式说法。

normal.en: In business news, a haemorrhage of cash or staff means rapid loss.
normal.cn: 在商业新闻里，haemorrhage of cash 或 staff 表示迅速流失。

abstract.en: Picture a red pipe that cracks and pours water into the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一根红色的水管裂开，水不断淌到街上。

abstract.en: Imagine a nurse pressing a clean pad hard on a wound until the flow stops.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把干净纱布紧紧压在伤口上，直到血不再流。

abstract.en: See a company as a body whose cash leaks out like blood through a cut.
abstract.cn: 把公司想象成身体，现金像血一样从切口流走。

examples.en: A severe haemorrhage can kill within minutes if it is not stopped.
examples.cn: 严重的大出血如果止不住，几分钟内就可能致命。

examples.en: Internal haemorrhage is often hard to detect at first.
examples.cn: 内出血在起初往往很难发现。

examples.en: The team was haemorrhaging talent to bigger firms.
examples.cn: 这支团队的人才正在大量流向更大的公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑帽瑞吉」——黑帽子里渗出血，一路往下淌：大出血；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 haima（血）+ rhegnynai（迸裂、爆出）→ haimorragia（血流迸出）→ 医学拉丁语 haemorrhagia → 英语 haemorrhage，核心义「血冲破口子外流」。

sensesIntro.en: Haemorrhage starts with the physical burst of blood, then the act of stopping it, next the figurative loss of money or people, and finally the verb and the metaphorical warning sign.
sensesIntro.cn: haemorrhage 先指血的物理性迸流，再指止血这一行为，接着引申为金钱或人的流失，最后落到动词用法与比喻性的警示信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pipe that cracks and cannot stop pouring.
core.cn: 核心意象：裂开的水管，怎么都止不住地往外淌。

branches.en: The medical core is a heavy flow of blood.
branches.cn: 医学核心义是大量流出的血。

branches.en: Handling the flow turns the noun into a controllable event.
branches.cn: 对血流进行处理，使这个名词变成可控的事件。

branches.en: Money, staff, and other valuables can drain away like blood.
branches.cn: 金钱、员工和其他宝贵资源可以像血一样流走。

branches.en: The verb makes the loss an ongoing, unstoppable action.
branches.cn: 动词用法让流失成为持续、止不住的过程。

branches.en: Bleeding signals a wound, so the metaphor points to hidden damage.
branches.cn: 流血意味着伤口，所以这个比喻指向隐藏的损害。

intro.en: Haemorrhage is built from Greek roots, with haemo- for blood and the rare ending -rrhage for a bursting out.
intro.cn: haemorrhage 由希腊词根构成：haemo- 表示血，少见的词尾 -rrhage 表示迸出。

latinIntro.en: The word reached Latin first as medical haemorrhagia, from which French and English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词先以医学拉丁语 haemorrhagia 的形式进入拉丁语，法语和英语再从拉丁语借入。

items.example: The root haemo- heads words about blood.
items.exampleCN: 词根 haemo- 位于与血有关的词开头。

items.example: American style writes the root as hemo-.
items.exampleCN: 美式拼写把该词根写作 hemo-。

items.example: The ending -rrhage names a sudden flowing out.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -rrhage 表示突然流出。

items.example: Haemorrhage keeps the medical sense.
items.exampleCN: haemorrhage 保留医学含义。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms haemorrhagic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 haemorrhagic。

items.example: Haemorrhagic describes a disease that bleeds.
items.exampleCN: haemorrhagic 描述会出血的疾病。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun haemorrhaging.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 haemorrhaging。

items.example: Haemorrhaging names the ongoing loss.
items.exampleCN: haemorrhaging 指持续进行的流失。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms haemorrhaged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 haemorrhaged。

items.meaning: the red pigment that carries oxygen in blood
items.example: Haemoglobin pairs the blood root with globin.
items.exampleCN: haemoglobin 把血词根与 globin 组合在一起。

definition_zh: 讨价还价；争价；为细节争论不休；勉强应对
definition_en: to argue about a price until an agreement is reached, or to argue over small details
core_image: 两张嘴在摊位两边来回砍价，价钱被一点点磨低
scene: 集市上，摊主说这件毛衣要二十块，顾客嫌贵，两人你来我往地争了好一会儿。They haggled over the price for ten minutes before shaking hands.
sceneCN: 这里 haggle 是「讨价还价」（第 1 个义项：买卖双方就价格反复争论直到成交）；句意：他们为价钱争了十分钟，然后握手成交。

pos.zh: 把价格砍低；讨价还价后得到

collocations.zh: 不停砍价，把价钱压到最低

derivatives.zh: 由 haggle 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「讨价还价；争价行为」
由 haggle 加表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「爱讨价还价的人」

senses.title: To bargain over a price
senses.definition: to argue with a seller or buyer over the price of something until both sides agree
senses.definitionCN: 与卖家或买家就某物价格反复争论，直到双方都接受
senses.example: She haggled with the trader over a silk scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 她和摊主为一条丝巾讨价还价。
senses.why: The word has always implied cutting something down with repeated blows, so a price is whittled down by argument the way a branch is chopped to size.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一开始就含有「反复挥动砍削」的意思，所以价格像树枝一样被一次次争论「砍」到合适的尺寸。

senses.title: To bring a price down by bargaining
senses.definition: to reach a lower price than first asked by bargaining hard
senses.definitionCN: 通过使劲讨价还价，把成交价压到低于最初要价的水平
senses.example: He haggled the price down to half what they wanted.
senses.exampleCN: 他把价钱砍到了对方要价的一半。
senses.why: If the core act is to hack away at a price, the natural result sense is the lower figure that remains when the cutting stops.
senses.whyCN: 如果核心动作是对价格「一刀刀地砍」，那么自然引申出的结果义就是砍完之后落到更低的那个价钱。

senses.title: To argue over small details
senses.definition: to spend time arguing about minor terms or details instead of agreeing
senses.definitionCN: 把时间花在小条款、小细节的争论上，迟迟达不成一致
senses.example: The two sides haggled for days over every clause.
senses.exampleCN: 双方为每一条款争论了好几天。
senses.why: Bargaining over a few coins and quarrelling over a few words feel the same: small things are picked apart one by one.
senses.whyCN: 为几个硬币讨价还价，和为几个字眼争吵，感觉是一样的：小事被一件件挑开来争。

senses.title: To argue in a tedious, petty way
senses.titleCN: 没完没了地争辩；斤斤计较
senses.definition: to keep arguing in a worrying, tiresome manner, often about things that hardly matter
senses.definitionCN: 以烦人、磨人的方式不停地争辩，常常为无关紧要的事
senses.example: We wasted the meeting haggling over wording.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把会议时间浪费在争论措辞上。
senses.why: An early English sense of the word meant to mangle or mumble, so haggling kept a hint of noise and irritation; the speaker sounds displeased.
senses.whyCN: 早期英语中这个词有「乱砍、含糊咕哝」的意思，所以 haggle 保留了噪音与烦躁的味道；说话人总带着不满。

senses.title: To struggle with a difficulty
senses.definition: to cope awkwardly or with difficulty with a task or a problem
senses.definitionCN: 笨拙地、勉强地应付某项任务或难题
senses.example: The old truck haggled up the steep hill.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧卡车艰难地爬上了陡坡。
senses.why: Chopping and cutting are rough, uneven work, so the word also described awkward, jerky movement and effortful coping.
senses.whyCN: 砍削是粗重、不匀称的活儿，所以这个词也用来形容笨拙、一顿一顿的动作和费力的应付。

senses.title: To cut up roughly
senses.definition: an older dialect sense: to cut or chop something in an uneven, careless way
senses.definitionCN: 较早的方言义：不均匀、粗心地砍削某物
senses.example: The old records show haggles for cutting wood badly.
senses.exampleCN: 旧记录中可见 haggles 表示把木头砍得乱七八糟。
senses.why: Behind the price argument lies the physical act of hacking, which survives in regional and old usage as chopping roughly.
senses.whyCN: 讨价还价的背后是实体「乱砍」的动作，这一原始义以粗砍的意思保留在方言和旧用法里。

intro.en: Haggle is probably from an old northern English verb hag, to chop, and it carried the idea of cutting down into the world of prices.
intro.cn: haggle 一般认为来自英格兰北部古动词 hag（砍），把「砍削削减」的意象带进了价格领域。

items.en: A reconstructed root for chopping or hacking lies behind the verb.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示砍切的重构词根是该动词的源头。

items.en: A verb meaning to cut or hack is recorded in Old English dialect.
items.cn: 古英语方言中记录有一个表示砍切的动词。

items.en: Hagge appears in northern writings meaning to chop or mangle.
items.cn: 十六世纪时，hagge 在北部的文字中出现，意为砍切、糟蹋。

items.en: Haggle is applied to tedious arguing and then to bargaining.
items.cn: haggle 先是用来表示令人厌烦的争辩，随后用于讨价还价。

items.en: Haggle settles as the everyday word for bargaining over a price.
items.cn: haggle 最终固定为「就价格讨价还价」的日常用语。

note.en: Haggle belongs to the market word family of bargain and barter, and looks close to haggle-related nouns such as haggler.
note.cn: haggle 属于 bargain、barter 这一「买卖议价」词族，与 haggler 等本族词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of arguing about a price
entries.definitionCN: 讨价还价的行为

entries.definition: a person who haggles a lot
entries.definitionCN: 爱讨价还价的人

entries.definition: an ugly old woman; has no link to haggling
entries.definitionCN: 丑老太婆；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to discuss a price or terms with someone
entries.definitionCN: 讨价还价；谈判

entries.definition: to exchange goods instead of paying money
entries.definitionCN: 以物易物

entries.definition: to discuss formally to reach an agreement
entries.definitionCN: 正式谈判；协商

normalIntro.en: Haggle grew from a chopping verb, so remembering the hack-and-cut picture gives you both the price sense and the petty-arguing sense.
normalIntro.cn: haggle 由「砍削」的动词发展而来，记住挥刀乱砍的画面，价格义和琐碎争吵义就都串起来了。

normal.en: Haggle is most common with over: haggle over a price.
normal.cn: haggle 最常见的搭配是 over：haggle over a price。

normal.en: Haggling is different from a firm discount: it happens before you pay.
normal.cn: haggling 与固定折扣不同：它发生在付款之前。

normal.en: A haggler asks, complains, and offers again until the number drops.
normal.cn: haggler 反复询问、抱怨、再出价，直到数字降下来。

normal.en: Haggle can mean to argue over details, not only money.
normal.cn: haggle 不限于钱，也可指为细节争论。

normal.en: In many markets haggling is normal, while in shops the price is fixed.
normal.cn: 在很多市场上砍价是常态，而商店里的价格是固定的。

abstract.en: Picture a saw going back and forth over the same price tag.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锯子在同一个价签上来回锯。

abstract.en: See a coin in the middle of a table, each buyer and seller pulling it their way.
abstract.cn: 想象桌子中间放着一枚硬币，买卖双方各往自己这边拉。

abstract.en: Think of two people chipping at a price with small tools until the edge is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人用小工具一点点凿掉价钱的边角。

examples.en: Tourists often pay too much because they do not haggle.
examples.cn: 游客常因为不砍价而多花钱。

examples.en: The two companies haggled over the small print for weeks.
examples.cn: 两家公司为细则争论了好几周。

examples.en: He is a good haggler when he buys antiques.
examples.cn: 他买古董时是个砍价好手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扛哥」——扛着东西跟老板磨价，一分一分往下磨：讨价还价；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语北部方言 hag（砍、砍削）→ 中古英语 hagge（乱砍、糟蹋）→ haggle（为小事争个不停→讨价还价），核心义「一遍遍砍削，把东西削减下来」。

sensesIntro.en: Haggle begins with bargaining over a price, narrows to the lower price won, widens to argument over details, then to petty quarrelling, and keeps its older rough-cutting sense at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: haggle 先指就价格争论，再指压下来的成交价，接着扩展到细节之争与斤斤计较，最边缘保留着「乱砍」的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people chopping at the same price tag from both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人从两边对同一个价签来回砍。

branches.en: The price argument is the everyday centre of the word.
branches.cn: 价格之争是这个词的日常核心。

branches.en: The chopped-down price is the result of the bargaining.
branches.cn: 被砍下来的价格是讨价还价的结果。

branches.en: Small details are treated like small coins and argued over one by one.
branches.cn: 小细节被当作小铜板，一件件地争。

branches.en: Rough hacking also describes jerky, effortful coping.
branches.cn: 粗重的砍削也用来形容一顿一顿、费力的应付。

branches.en: The old chopping sense is the physical origin of the price sense.
branches.cn: 旧的「砍」义是价格义的实体来源。

intro.en: Haggle is a native English verb with no borrowed prefixes, forming nouns with -ing and -er instead.
intro.cn: haggle 是英语本族动词，没有借来的前缀，靠 -ing 和 -er 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: Haggle is Germanic in origin rather than Latin, so it has no direct Latin relative and the list of same-family Latin forms is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: haggle 源出日耳曼语而非拉丁语，没有直接的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁同源词清单留空。

items.example: The root hag- gives the chopping picture.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hag- 提供砍削的画面。

items.example: Haggle keeps the cutting sense in prices.
items.exampleCN: haggle 把砍削的意味留在价格上。

items.example: The ending -le suggests repeated small cuts.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 暗示一再的小幅砍切。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The ending -ing forms the noun haggling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 haggling。

items.example: The suffix -er forms haggler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 haggler。

items.example: Haggling happens before the deal is closed.
items.exampleCN: haggling 发生在成交之前。

items.example: A haggler enjoys the argument itself.
items.exampleCN: haggler 享受争论本身。

items.example: Haggle down means to force a lower price.
items.exampleCN: haggle down 表示把价钱压到更低。

definition_zh: 使神圣；把……奉为神圣；尊崇；圣徒
definition_en: to make something or someone holy and worthy of deep respect, or to treat something as sacred
core_image: 一双手把一盏旧灯举过头顶，灯被罩上神圣的光
scene: 小镇的老教堂建于几百年前，人们把它当作最神圣的地方，进门要放轻脚步。The villagers hallow the old church with quiet respect every time they enter.
sceneCN: 这里 hallow 是「使……神圣、把……奉为神圣」（第 1 个义项：被敬为神圣、专属于神圣）；句意：村民每次走进老教堂，都以安静的敬意把它奉为神圣。

pos.zh: 圣徒（多用复数，节名中常见）

collocations.zh: 使某地神圣；奉某地为圣地
愿你的名受尊崇（主祷文名句）

derivatives.zh: 由 hallow 加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「神圣的；受人尊崇的」
由 hallow 与 mass（弥撒）复合而成，义为「诸圣节」
由 hallow 与 tide（时节）复合而成，义为「诸圣节前后时期」

senses.title: To make something holy
senses.definition: to set something or someone apart as holy and fit for sacred use
senses.definitionCN: 把某物或某人分别出来，视为神圣、专供神圣之用
senses.example: Pilgrims believe the spring was hallowed by a saint.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者相信这眼泉水因圣人而变得神圣。
senses.why: Old English hal meant whole, sound, and holy, so to hallow was to make a thing whole and set apart, with nothing ordinary left about it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hal 兼有「完整、健全、神圣」之意，所以 hallow 是把一物「使其完整并分别出来」，不再属于寻常之列。

senses.title: To show deep respect
senses.definition: to treat something as worthy of great reverence and honour
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物当作值得极大敬畏与敬意的东西来对待
senses.example: The nation hallows the memory of its first settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家崇敬地铭记最早的定居者。
senses.why: When what is holy is also dear, honouring it becomes an act of reverence: to hallow is to hold something above ordinary talk.
senses.whyCN: 当神圣之物同时被人珍视，敬奉它便成了一种崇敬之举：hallow 就是把某物抬到寻常言谈之上。

senses.title: A saint or holy person
senses.definition: an old noun use: a holy person, especially a saint honoured by the church
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法：神圣的人，尤指受教会敬奉的圣徒
senses.example: All Hallows, the feast of the saints, gave us Halloween.
senses.exampleCN: 诸圣节指圣徒的节日，halloween 一词就由它而来。
senses.why: The same root also supplied a noun for a holy person, so all hallows means all the saints, and their eve became Halloween.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根还派生出指神圣之人的名词，所以 all hallows 即「诸圣」，其前夜就演变为 Halloween。

senses.title: To bless or make sacred by words
senses.definition: to declare something sacred in a prayer or blessing, or to set it aside for God
senses.definitionCN: 在祈祷或祝福中宣告某物神圣，或把它归给神使用
senses.example: The priest hallowed the new chapel in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天里，神父为新的小礼拜堂祝圣。
senses.why: A blessing is spoken out loud, and the word took on the act of making holy by voice, close to consecrate and sanctify.
senses.whyCN: 祝福是要说出口的，这个词因此也指以言语使之神圣，与 consecrate、sanctify 相近。

senses.title: Fitted for special honour
senses.definition: adjective use: made sacred, or deeply respected because of long usage or belief
senses.definitionCN: 形容词用法：被视为神圣的，或因长期习俗与信仰而深受尊敬
senses.example: They walked in silence across hallowed ground.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沉默地走过这片神圣之地。
senses.why: The participle hallowed turned into an adjective, so the act of making holy also describes the result: ground that is now holy.
senses.whyCN: 分词 hallowed 凝固为形容词，所以「使神圣」这一动作同时也描述结果：一块如今已属神圣的土地。

senses.title: Preserved in set phrases
senses.definition: a surviving verb use, mainly in prayers and the fixed phrase hallowed be thy name
senses.definitionCN: 残存的动词用法，主要用于祷告与固定短语 hallowed be thy name
senses.example: The prayer begins in an older tone that still hallows the name.
senses.exampleCN: 这段祷文以更古拙的语气开头，依然在尊崇那名。
senses.why: In daily speech the verb faded as holy and blame took over, but prayers kept it alive for listeners.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，随着 holy 取代旧义，这个动词渐渐淡出，但祷文让它一直存留在听众耳中。

intro.en: Hallow comes from Old English halgian, to make holy, from hal, whole and holy, a word shared with holy and heal.
intro.cn: hallow 来自古英语 halgian（使神圣），源于 hal（完整、神圣），与 holy、heal 同出一源。

items.en: A reconstructed root for whole and sound lies behind the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「完整、完好」的重构词根是这一词族的源头。

items.en: Hal mean whole and holy, and halgian means to make holy.
items.cn: 古英语 hal 意为完整、神圣，halgian 意为使神圣。

items.en: Hallows names the saints, and All Hallows becomes a fixed feast.
items.cn: 中古英语中 hallows 指诸圣，all hallows 成为固定的节日名称。

items.en: Holy and the adjective hallowed take over, and the verb grows rare.
items.cn: 到了十六世纪，holy 与形容词 hallowed 接过主要用法，动词本身变得少见。

items.en: Hallowed survives in prayers and in set phrases such as hallowed ground.
items.cn: hallowed 存留于祷文与 hallowed ground 这类固定说法中。

note.en: Hallow is the verb behind holy and hallowed, and it sits beside bless, sanctify, and consecrate in the word field of sacred things.
note.cn: hallow 是 holy 与 hallowed 背后的动词，在「神圣」这一语义场里与 bless、sanctify、consecrate 相邻。

entries.definition: made holy or deeply respected
entries.definitionCN: 神圣的；受人尊崇的

entries.definition: sacred, set apart for God
entries.definitionCN: 神圣的；圣洁的

entries.definition: empty inside; has a different origin
entries.definitionCN: 中空的；只是拼写与发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make holy with a prayer
entries.definitionCN: 祝福；使神圣

entries.definition: to make something holy or sacred
entries.definitionCN: 使神圣；使圣洁

entries.definition: to set something apart as sacred
entries.definitionCN: 奉献；使成为神圣

normalIntro.en: Hallow belongs to the same family as holy and heal: the old root meant whole, so making holy is making whole and setting apart.
normalIntro.cn: hallow 与 holy、heal 同出一族：古词根意为「完整」，所以「使之神圣」就是把事物变得完整并分别出来。

normal.en: The root hal means whole and holy, giving both hallow and holy.
normal.cn: 词根 hal 意为完整、神圣，既生成 hallow 也生成 holy。

normal.en: Hallowed is now far more common than the verb hallow.
normal.cn: 如今 hallowed 比动词 hallow 常见得多。

normal.en: All Hallows means all the saints, and its eve gave Halloween.
normal.cn: all hallows 指诸圣，其前夜演变为 Halloween。

normal.en: Hallowed ground is land treated as sacred, often by age or sacrifice.
normal.cn: hallowed ground 指被视为神圣的土地，常因年代久远或牺牲而得名。

normal.en: Contrast hallowed with hollow, which means empty inside.
normal.cn: 把 hallowed 与 hollow（中空的）对比记忆，两者形近而义异。

abstract.en: Picture a priest lifting a lamp and letting a golden light cover it.
abstract.cn: 想象神职人员举起一盏灯，让金色的光将它笼罩。

abstract.en: See people taking off their shoes as they cross into one small area of ground.
abstract.cn: 想象人们踏进一小块土地时脱下了鞋。

abstract.en: Think of a stone marked with the names of saints, lit by candles.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刻着圣徒名字、被烛光照亮的石碑。

examples.en: The poem calls the battlefield hallowed ground.
examples.cn: 这首诗把这片战场称为神圣之地。

examples.en: Some traditions hallow the day of the dead.
examples.cn: 有些传统把亡灵之日奉为神圣。

examples.en: He spoke of his teacher with hallowing respect.
examples.cn: 他谈起老师时怀着近乎崇敬的敬意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈喽」——双手合十说一声哈喽，把地方奉为神圣：使神圣、尊崇；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 halgian（使神圣）← hal（完整、健全、神圣）→ 英语 hallow；与 holy、heal、whole 同源，核心义「使之完整而分别出来，成为神圣」。

sensesIntro.en: Hallow starts with making a thing holy, moves to reverent honouring, gives a noun for saints, then blessing by words, and finally survives as the adjective hallowed and in prayers.
sensesIntro.cn: hallow 先指使某物神圣，再引申为怀着敬意地尊崇，并派生出指圣徒的名词，随后指以言语祝圣，最后以形容词 hallowed 与祷文形式存留至今。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands lifting a lamp into golden light.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一盏灯举到金色的光里。

branches.en: Making a thing holy is the original verb sense.
branches.cn: 使某物神圣是这个动词的本义。

branches.en: Reverence turns the sacred act into a way of honouring.
branches.cn: 敬畏把神圣的举动变成一种敬奉方式。

branches.en: The saint noun and the blessing both come from holy.
branches.cn: 圣徒名词与祝福义都出自「神圣」这一根本。

branches.en: The participle describes the result of the act.
branches.cn: 分词形式描述动作造成的结果。

branches.en: Prayer keeps the old verb alive in set phrases.
branches.cn: 祷文让这个旧动词在固定短语里延续。

intro.en: Hallow is a native English word built on the Old English root hal, with the verb ending -ow.
intro.cn: hallow 是英语本族词，建立在古英语词根 hal 之上，动词结尾为 -ow。

latinIntro.en: Hallow is Germanic, but Latin words for sacred things such as sacer and sanctus offer useful sacred relatives.
latinIntro.cn: hallow 属日耳曼语，不过拉丁语中表示神圣的 sacer、sanctus 等词提供了有用的「神圣」近亲。

items.example: The root hal- carries the idea of wholeness.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hal- 承载「完整」这一概念。

items.meaning: a verb ending kept from Old English
items.meaningCN: 沿自古英语的动词结尾
items.example: The ending -ow shapes a verb from the root.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ow 把词根塑造成动词。

items.example: Hallow keeps the old verb sense.
items.exampleCN: hallow 保留古老的动词含义。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms hallowed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 hallowed。

items.example: The suffix -ows forms hallows.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ows 构成 hallows。

items.meaning: a religious feast such as All Hallows
items.meaningCN: 诸圣节一类的宗教节日
items.example: The suffix -mas forms hallowmas.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -mas 构成 hallowmas。

items.example: The suffix -tide forms hallowtide.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tide 构成 hallowtide。

items.example: Holy shares the root hal- with hallow.
items.exampleCN: holy 与 hallow 共享词根 hal-。

items.meaning: to make whole and sound again
items.example: Heal keeps the old sense of wholeness.
items.exampleCN: heal 保留「完整」的古老含义。

definition_zh: 门厅；走廊；过道
definition_en: a passage inside a building that leads from room to room, often starting at the front door
core_image: 推开家门先走进一条长长的过道，两侧是紧闭的房门，尽头亮着一盏灯
