scene: 客人刚走进公寓，换鞋还没换完，就被引到过道尽头那扇亮着灯的门前。The guest stepped into a narrow hallway and followed her host to the far door.
sceneCN: 这里 hallway 指「房屋内部连接各房间的过道」（第 1 个义项：房屋内连接房间的过道）；句意为客人走进一条狭窄的过道，跟着主人走向尽头那扇门。可辨识物件：鞋架、两侧房门、尽头的灯。

derivatives.zh: 大厅；门厅；礼堂：hallway 的第一部分，义域从殿堂收窄到住宅内的过道
楼道；通道：与 hallway 同义域，多见于英式与建筑文献，并非由 hallway 派生

senses.title: Passage inside a house
senses.definition: a passage inside a house that links the front door and the rooms
senses.definitionCN: 住宅内部连接前门与各房间的通道
senses.example: The hallway runs from the front door past the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这条过道从前门一直通到厨房。
senses.why: Hall first named a large covered space; -way (road, path) narrows it to the route you walk inside a house.
senses.whyCN: hall 最初指有顶的大空间，加 -way「路、通道」后收窄为住宅里可以行走的那条路线。

senses.title: Corridor of a public building
senses.definition: a corridor in a school, hotel, hospital or office building
senses.definitionCN: 学校、酒店、医院或办公楼里的走廊
senses.example: Students waited in the hallway outside the exam room.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在考场外的走廊上等候。
senses.why: The same passage idea extends from the private house to any shared building.
senses.whyCN: 同样的通道概念从私人住宅扩展到任何共用的建筑。

senses.title: Entrance passage or foyer
senses.definition: the small area just inside the front door where guests arrive
senses.definitionCN: 前门内供客人进入的小空间
senses.example: She left her wet umbrella in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 她把手上的湿雨伞放在了门厅。
senses.why: The start of the passage, nearest the door, is often the place where visitors are received.
senses.whyCN: 通道靠近大门的那一端，常成为接待来客的地方，于是单独获得「门厅」之意。

intro.en: Hallway is an English compound of hall, a Germanic word for a large roofed space, and way, the path you walk.
intro.cn: hallway 是英语复合词，由 hall（日耳曼语中表示有大屋顶的室内空间的词）与 way（行走的路线）组合而成。

items.en: Heall named a large covered building or hall, from a Germanic root related to cover.
items.cn: heall 指有顶的大建筑或大厅，词源可追溯到表示「遮盖」的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Weg meant a road, track or path, and still survives in highway, pathway and doorway.
items.cn: weg 意为道路、小径或路线，至今保留在 highway、pathway、doorway 等词中。

items.en: Hall broadened from a great room to any passage or entrance room in a house.
items.cn: 在英语中 hall 由大厅扩展为住宅内的任何过道或入口房间。

items.en: Hallway appears as a compound naming the passage that connects rooms in a house.
items.cn: hallway 作为复合词出现，指连接住宅各房间的通道。

items.en: American English made hallway the ordinary word for the corridor of a school, hotel or hospital.
items.cn: 美式英语使 hallway 成为学校、酒店或医院走廊的常用词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact century of the compound is approximate, but the source of both parts is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：复合词形成的确切世纪为约数，但两部分的来源都确定。

note.en: Group one holds words that share hall or the -way ending; group two holds other words for a passage.
note.cn: 第一组是与 hall 或 -way 词尾有关的词；第二组是其它表示「通道」的词。

entries.definition: a large room, especially one used for meetings or public events
entries.definitionCN: 大厅；礼堂：hallway 的第一部分，通常指用于会议或公共活动的大房间。

entries.definition: a typical feature or the official stamp of quality
entries.definitionCN: 标志；品质印记：只是拼写以 hall- 开头，词源与 hallway 无关。

entries.definition: the opening in a wall where a door is fitted
entries.definitionCN: 门口；门洞：与 hallway 共享 -way「通道」这一构词成分。

entries.definition: a firefighting tool used to force open doors and walls
entries.definitionCN: 哈利根撬棍（一种消防破拆工具）：只是拼写开头相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a long passage from which rooms open
entries.definitionCN: 走廊：英式常用词，义域与 hallway 高度重合。

entries.definition: a narrow way that allows movement from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 通道：比 hallway 更宽泛的通道说法。

entries.definition: the entrance area of a hotel or theatre
entries.definitionCN: 门厅：常指酒店或剧院的入口大厅，比 hallway 更正式。

entries.definition: the flat area at the top of a set of stairs
entries.definitionCN: 楼梯平台：常与走廊相连，但本身指楼梯尽头的平台。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real parts hall and -way, the real compounds in the family and the real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想依靠真实的构词成分 hall 与 -way、词族中的真实复合词以及真实搭配。

normal.en: Hall is a big roofed room; -way is a path, so a hallway is the path inside a building.
normal.cn: hall 是有屋顶的大房间，-way 是小路，合成后就是建筑物内部的通道。

normal.en: The same -way ending builds highway, pathway and doorway.
normal.cn: 同一个 -way 词尾还构成 highway、pathway 与 doorway。

normal.en: British speakers often say corridor where American speakers say hallway.
normal.cn: 同样指走廊，英式多说 corridor，美式多说 hallway。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: down the hallway, at the end of the hallway, in the hallway.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：沿着走廊往里、在走廊尽头、在走廊里。

normal.en: Do not confuse hall, the big room, with hallway, the narrow way that leads to it.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 hall（大厅）与 hallway（通向大厅的那条窄通道）。

abstract.en: Picture a long thin strip of floor with front doors on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的地板，两侧都开着一扇扇房门。

abstract.en: Picture the hallway light left on so that the last person home can find the switch.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊上的灯留着不关，好让最晚回家的人找到开关。

abstract.en: Picture footsteps echoing on bare boards after everyone else has gone to bed.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都睡了以后，脚步在空木地板上回响。

examples.en: The hotel hallway was lined with prints of old maps.
examples.cn: 酒店的走廊两侧挂满了古地图的复制画。

examples.en: He heard the kettle whistle down the short hallway.
examples.cn: 他沿短短的过道听见水壶的哨声。

examples.en: Two bicycles were parked in the hallway again.
examples.cn: 又有两辆自行车停在了走廊里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「霍尔伟」——霍尔老先生的房子有几条过道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: heall（有顶的大厅）+ weg（道路）→ hall（门厅；大厅）+ -way（通道）→ hallway（过道）；两部分的词源都确定。

sensesIntro.en: Hallway moves one short step from the passage inside a house, to the shared corridors of public buildings, and back to the entry area by the front door.
sensesIntro.cn: hallway 只走了一小步：从住宅内部的过道，到公共建筑里共用的走廊，再回到前门旁的门厅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow floor between two rows of doors.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排房门之间一条狭长的地板。

branches.en: HOME ROUTE: the passage that links the rooms of a private house.
branches.cn: 家中的路线：连接私人住宅各房间的通道。

branches.en: SHARED BUILDING: the same route appears in schools, hotels and hospitals.
branches.cn: 共用建筑：同一条路线出现在学校、酒店与医院里。

branches.en: DOOR FIRST: the end near the front door becomes a place of arrival.
branches.cn: 先见其门：靠近前门的一端成为抵达之地。

branches.en: The entrance end of the house passage is also where guests are met.
branches.cn: 住宅过道靠门的一端，也正是迎接客人的地方。

branches.en: In hotels the corridor and the entrance area often meet at the front desk.
branches.cn: 在酒店里，走廊与入口区常在接待台处相接。

intro.en: Hallway is a Germanic-English compound, not a Latin derivative; its parts are hall and the suffix-like element -way.
intro.cn: hallway 是日耳曼语来源的英语复合词，并非拉丁语派生词；其构词成分是 hall 与类似后缀的 -way。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for the path element; the classical word for a running corridor is ambulacrum or cryptoporticus.
latinIntro.cn: 通道部分的来源不是拉丁语；拉丁语中表示狭长通道的说法是 ambulacrum 或 cryptoporticus。

items.example: The hall was packed for the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里挤满了开会的人。

items.example: Doorway and pathway share this ending.
items.exampleCN: doorway 与 pathway 共享这个结尾。

items.example: The hallway leads to the bedrooms.
items.exampleCN: 这条过道通向几间卧室。

items.example: The halls and hallways were repainted.
items.exampleCN: 大厅与各条走廊都重新粉刷了。

items.example: Switch the hallway light off last.
items.exampleCN: 最后一个关掉走廊灯。

items.meaning: also used in compounds for school or hospital routes
items.meaningCN: 也用于学校或医院路线的复合说法
items.example: The school hallway was quiet during the test.
items.exampleCN: 考试期间学校走廊很安静。

items.example: He stood in the doorway.
items.exampleCN: 他站在门口。

items.example: The highway runs along the coast.
items.exampleCN: 公路沿着海岸延伸。

items.example: A narrow corridor links the two wings.
items.exampleCN: 一条窄走廊连接两翼。

definition_zh: 卤素；卤族元素
definition_en: any of the chemically related non-metal elements of group seventeen of the periodic table, which form salts with metals
core_image: 盐罐旁边并排放着几只灯泡状的元素符号，它们一碰到金属就结成盐
scene: 实验室的柜子里并排放着几只棕色小瓶，标签写着不同的元素符号，旁边备注着它们都能与钠结成盐。In the lab we studied how each halogen forms a salt with sodium.
sceneCN: 这里 halogen 是化学术语，指「能与金属结成盐的一族元素」（第 1 个义项：卤族元素）；句意为我们在实验室研究了每种卤素如何与钠结成盐。可辨识物件：棕色试剂瓶、元素符号标签、成盐的提示。

derivatives.zh: 卤化物：由 -ide 后缀构成，指卤素与另一元素形成的二元化合物
卤化的：halogen + -ated 构成，表示已引入卤素原子的物质
卤化反应：由动词 halogenate 加 -ion 构成
卤素互化物之间的：由 inter-「之间」加 halogen 构成

senses.title: An element of the halogen group
senses.definition: any of the five related non-metal elements fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine
senses.definitionCN: 氟、氯、溴、碘、砹这五种化学性质相近的非金属元素之一
senses.example: Each halogen has one spare electron in its outer shell.
senses.exampleCN: 每一种卤素的原子外层都多出一个电子。
senses.why: Greek hals (salt) plus -gen (producer) names the group by what its members produce with metals.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hals「盐」加 -gen「产生者」，按这族元素与金属成盐的能力来命名。

senses.title: Halogen used as a mass noun
senses.definition: the group of elements taken as a class, without a plural
senses.definitionCN: 把这一族元素作为一个类别来指称，通常不加复数
senses.example: Fluorine is the most reactive element in halogen chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 在卤素化学里，氟是最活泼的元素。
senses.why: Chemists often speak of the group as one substance, so the singular is used without an article.
senses.whyCN: 化学家常把整族当作一个类别来谈，因此用单数且不加冠词。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: describing a lamp, compound or reaction that uses or contains a halogen
senses.definitionCN: 形容使用或含有卤素的灯、化合物或反应
senses.example: A halogen lamp gives a bright, slightly warm light.
senses.exampleCN: 卤素灯发出明亮而略偏暖的光。
senses.why: The noun is pressed into attributive use, as in halogen lamp or halogen compound.
senses.whyCN: 名词被借作定语，如 halogen lamp、halogen compound 之类说法。

senses.title: Halogen in everyday domestic use
senses.definition: the common name for halogen lamps and bulbs in household lighting
senses.definitionCN: 家用照明里对卤素灯与卤素灯泡的俗称
senses.example: Replace the halogen bulb with an efficient one.
senses.exampleCN: 把这只卤素灯泡换成节能的。
senses.why: The technical group name shrank to a shop label because these lamps became common household items.
senses.whyCN: 这种灯成了普通家用物品，「卤素」于是从化学术语缩成了商店标签。

senses.title: Halogenated substances
senses.definition: in environmental writing, of chemicals that contain halogen atoms
senses.definitionCN: 在环境类写作中，指含有卤素原子的化学物质
senses.example: Halogenated solvents require careful disposal.
senses.exampleCN: 含卤溶剂需要小心处理。
senses.why: The element name lends itself to the adjective halogenated when the focus is on added halogen atoms.
senses.whyCN: 当关注点落在被引入的卤素原子上时，元素名就派生出形容词 halogenated。

intro.en: Halogen is a modern scientific coinage built from Greek hals (salt) and the suffix -gen (producer).
intro.cn: halogen 是近代科学新造的词，由希腊语 hals「盐」与词尾 -gen「产生者」构成。

items.en: Hals meant salt, and the family salts that the group forms with metals sit behind the name.
items.cn: hals 意为盐，这族元素与金属生成的盐类正是命名的依据。

items.en: French chemists coined the group name from the salt-forming property of chlorine.
items.cn: 法国化学家根据氯的成盐特性，创造了这一族元素的名称。

items.en: The word entered English chemistry as the name of a family related to chlorine.
items.cn: 该词进入英语化学语汇，最初指与氯相近的一族元素。

items.en: New members were added to the group and the name came to cover the family of elements.
items.cn: 随着新元素被发现并入族，这个词逐渐涵盖整族元素。

items.en: Industrial lighting made the compound halogen lamp familiar outside the laboratory.
items.cn: 工业照明的普及使 halogen lamp 这样的说法走出实验室。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact year of the English first use is approximate; the Greek parts are settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：英语首见的确切年份为约数，希腊语构词成分则已确定。

note.en: Group one holds chemical words that share the -gen ending or the hal- shape; group two holds other terms of the same chemistry field.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 -gen 词尾或 hal- 字形的化学词；第二组是同一化学领域内的其他术语。

entries.definition: the lightest chemical element, named as the water producer
entries.definitionCN: 氢：最轻的化学元素，因能生成水而命名，与 halogen 共享 -gen 词尾。

entries.definition: rock salt, sodium chloride in mineral form
entries.definitionCN: 岩盐：氯化钠的矿物形态，与 halogen 共享希腊语「盐」的词根。

entries.definition: a compound of a halogen with another element
entries.definitionCN: 卤化物：卤素与另一元素生成的化合物，是 halogen 的直接派生词。

entries.definition: producing salt, or relating to halogens
entries.definitionCN: 生盐的；与卤素有关的：由 -ic 后缀构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a greenish gas that is the best-known member of the halogen group
entries.definitionCN: 氯：一种黄绿色气体，是卤族中最广为人知的成员。

entries.definition: the most reactive element of the halogen group
entries.definitionCN: 氟：卤族中反应最活泼的元素。

entries.definition: an element that does not conduct heat or electricity well
entries.definitionCN: 非金属：导热导电性差的元素，卤素属于这一大类。

entries.definition: an incandescent lamp filled with a halogen gas
entries.definitionCN: 卤素灯：充有卤素气体的白炽灯。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real Greek parts, the real element family and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想依靠真实的希腊构词成分、真实的元素族以及真实复合词。

normal.en: hals is salt and -gen is producer: halogens are the salt producers.
normal.cn: hals 是盐，-gen 是产生者，所以卤素就是「成盐的元素」。

normal.en: The group holds fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine, all in group seventeen.
normal.cn: 这一族包括氟、氯、溴、碘、砹，都在元素周期表第十七族。

normal.en: Hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen share the same -gen ending with different producers.
normal.cn: 氢、氧、氮与 halogen 共享 -gen 词尾，但「产生」的东西各不相同。

normal.en: A halide is a compound, while a halogen is one of the five elements.
normal.cn: halide 指化合物，halogen 指那五种元素本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: halogen lamp, halogen bulb, halogen group, free halogen.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：卤素灯、卤素灯泡、卤族、游离卤素。

abstract.en: Picture a salt shaker that also switches on like a light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盐罐，同时还能像灯一样亮起来。

abstract.en: Picture five differently coloured jars lined up under one label.
abstract.cn: 想象五个颜色各异的罐子排在同一张标签下。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that glows a little hotter and warmer than its neighbours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只灯比旁边的灯更容易发烫、颜色更暖。

examples.en: The halogen group sits at the right edge of the periodic table.
examples.cn: 卤族位于元素周期表的最右一列。

examples.en: A halogen lamp contains a small amount of reactive gas.
examples.cn: 卤素灯里含有少量活性气体。

examples.en: Bromine and iodine are both members of the halogens.
examples.cn: 溴和碘都是卤素成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈啰根」——打了招呼就结盐；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hals「盐」+ -gen「产生者」→ 法语化学家的近代科学造词 → 英语 halogen，核心义「成盐一族」。

sensesIntro.en: Halogen is one technical noun that settles into five uses: the element group, the uncountable class, the adjective, the household lamp and the environmental description of halogenated chemicals.
sensesIntro.cn: halogen 是一个技术名词，分化出五种用法：元素族名、集合名词、定语用法、家用灯具以及环境写作里的含卤说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of jars whose contents turn to salt when they touch a metal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排罐子，里面东西一碰到金属就结成盐。

branches.en: GROUP MEMBER: each of the five elements is a halogen.
branches.cn: 族内成员：五种元素中的每一种都是一个卤素。

branches.en: AS A CLASS: the whole group can be named in the singular.
branches.cn: 作为类别：整族可以用单数来指称。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTIVE: the noun shades into an adjective before lamp or compound.
branches.cn: 定语化：在 lamp、compound 之前，名词滑向形容词。

branches.en: Sodium chloride shows the group name in action: a halogen meets a metal and forms a salt.
branches.cn: 氯化钠正体现族名的逻辑：卤素遇到金属，生成盐。

branches.en: EVERYDAY USE: bulbs and halogenated solvents carry the technical name into ordinary life.
branches.cn: 日常用途：灯泡与含卤溶剂把技术名词带进日常生活。

intro.en: Halogen is built from two Greek elements, hal- (salt) and -gen (producer), then extended by English suffixes.
intro.cn: halogen 由两个希腊构词成分构成：hal-「盐」与 -gen「产生者」，其后又由英语后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Greek parts reach Latin science through the international word for salt, sal, and the compound suffix -ide.
latinIntro.cn: 这些希腊构词成分经由国际通用的「盐」这一词形进入拉丁科学词汇，也可能带出 -ide 这类化合物后缀。

items.example: The root hal- points to salt.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hal- 指向盐。

items.example: The suffix is shared by hydrogen and oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾与 hydrogen、oxygen 共用。

items.example: Chlorine is a halogen.
items.exampleCN: 氯是一种卤素。

items.example: The halogens grow darker down the group.
items.exampleCN: 这一族的卤素自上而下颜色越来越深。

items.example: Metal halides glow in flame tests.
items.exampleCN: 金属卤化物在焰色试验中会发光。

items.example: Halogenated compounds persist in soils.
items.exampleCN: 含卤化合物会在土壤中残留。

items.example: The prefix links members inside the group.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示族内成员之间的关系。

items.meaning: a compound of two different halogens
items.example: Chlorine fluoride is an interhalogen compound.
items.exampleCN: 氟化氯是一种卤素互化物。

items.example: The adjective describes salt forming elements.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述成盐的元素。

definition_zh: 把……减半；平分；对折
definition_en: to divide something into two equal parts, or to reduce it to half its amount
core_image: 一张纸被从中间对折，刀口正好落在正中央，两边一样大
scene: 妈妈把生日蛋糕从正中间切下去，让两个孩子一人一半。She halved the cake carefully so that each child got the same share.
sceneCN: 这里 halve 指「把某物分成相等的两半」（第 1 个义项：把东西平分）；句意为她小心地把蛋糕分成两半，让每个孩子得到一样多的一份。可辨识物件：蛋糕、正中的刀口、两只不同的盘子。

derivatives.zh: 一半；半的：halve 所依据的名词，减半就是得到 half
减半的：halve 加 -ed 构成的形容词形式
减半；对折：由动词加 -ing 构成的动名词

senses.title: Divide into two equal parts
senses.definition: to cut or separate something into two parts of the same size
senses.definitionCN: 把某物切成或分成大小相同的两部分
senses.example: She halved the cake carefully so that each child got the same share.
senses.exampleCN: 她小心地把蛋糕分成两半，让每个孩子得到一样多的一份。
senses.why: The verb was made from half, and its first job is to carry the object from one whole to two halves.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由 half 构成，最直接的作用就是把一个整体变成两个半份。

senses.title: Reduce to half the amount
senses.definition: to reduce a number, cost, time or amount to fifty per cent of what it was
senses.definitionCN: 把数量、成本、时间或总额减少到原来的百分之五十
senses.example: The new route halves the journey time to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线把去海边的旅程时间缩短了一半。
senses.why: Dividing into two equal parts becomes subtracting one of them when only the total matters.
senses.whyCN: 当关注的只是总量时，分成两半就等于拿走其中一半，于是产生「减到一半」的义项。

senses.title: Cut an object through the middle
senses.definition: to cut a solid object in two, as a ball, a lemon or a plank
senses.definitionCN: 把球、柠檬或木板之类的实物从中间切成两半
senses.example: Halve the lemons and squeeze them into a jug.
senses.exampleCN: 把柠檬切成两半，挤汁到壶里。
senses.why: This is the concrete kitchen and workshop version of sense one: the physical cut left visible.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项在厨房与工坊里的具体版本，刀口留在实物上。

senses.title: Become half in size
senses.definition: of a number, price or group: to become half as large, without a separate object
senses.definitionCN: 指数目、价格或群体自行减少一半，不带宾语
senses.example: The cost of solar panels has halved in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能板的成本在十年间减半。
senses.why: The intransitive use lets the thing itself change, as when a price falls to half.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法让事物自行发生变化，例如价格跌到一半。

senses.title: In golf, to draw a hole
senses.definition: in golf, to play a hole against an opponent with both players taking the same number of strokes
senses.definitionCN: 在高尔夫中与对手打同一洞，双方杆数相同
senses.example: Both players halved the long par four with par.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都以标准杆平分了这个长四杆洞。
senses.why: Draws split a point between two players, just as halves split an object.
senses.whyCN: 平局让两名选手各得一半分数，与把物体分成两半是同一思路。

intro.en: Halve is an English verb formed from the noun half, which comes from Old English healf, meaning a part or one of two sides.
intro.cn: halve 是由名词 half 构成的英语动词；half 来自古英语 healf，义为一部分或两侧之一。

items.en: The ancestor form is reconstructed as a word for half or a side, and no certain Indo-European root is agreed.
items.cn: 其祖语形式被重构为表示「一半、侧面」的词，但更远的印欧语词根没有公认结论。

items.en: Healf meant half or a side, and also gave half in modern English.
items.cn: healf 意为半或一侧，后来演变为现代英语的 half。

items.en: Halven grew up beside half as a verb of cutting and dividing.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，与 half 并行的动词 halven 出现，表示切割与分配。

items.en: Halve settled into its present spelling, with the silent l already lost in speech.
items.cn: 词形固定为 halve，l 在口语中早已不发音。

items.en: The verb spread to money, time, risk and statistics, where it means reducing to halfway.
items.cn: 该动词扩展到金钱、时间、风险与统计领域，表示减到一半。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Germanic origin of the half word is unsettled; the English history from healf is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：「半」这个词在日耳曼语之前的来源没有定论；从 healf 起的英语发展则确定。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the halv- / half- spelling; group two holds verbs of dividing and reducing.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 halv- 或 half- 形近部分的词；第二组是表示分割与减少的动词。

entries.definition: one of two equal parts of something
entries.definitionCN: 一半：halve 所依据的名词，也是它要得到的结果。

entries.definition: the plural of half, or the third person of the verb
entries.definitionCN: half 的复数，同时是 halve 的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: cut in two or reduced to half
entries.definitionCN: 被分成两半或被减半：halve 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: the home of a colony of bees
entries.definitionCN: 蜂箱：只是拼写与 halve 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to divide into parts, which need not be equal
entries.definitionCN: 分开：分成若干份，不要求相等。

entries.definition: to cut exactly in two, used of lines and angles
entries.definitionCN: 把……平分：几何学中指把线或角精确二等分。

entries.definition: to reduce an amount by an unspecified degree
entries.definitionCN: 削减：减少多少并不确定，不如 halve 精确。

entries.definition: to become or make twice as much
entries.definitionCN: 加倍：与 halve 方向相反。

normalIntro.en: These associations use the real link to half, the real verb forms and the real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想依靠与 half 的真实联系、真实的动词形式以及真实搭配。

normal.en: Halve is the verb built on half: to halve is to make half.
normal.cn: halve 是由 half 构成的动词：halve 就是「使其变成一半」。

normal.en: The third person halves is written with -ves, like leaf and leaves.
normal.cn: 第三人称 halves 把 f 写成 v，与 leaf、leaves 的变化相同。

normal.en: The past forms halved and halving keep the v sound; only the base falls back to the silent l.
normal.cn: 过去式 halved 与现在分词 halving 保留 v 音，只有原形里 l 不发音。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: halve the cost, halve the number, halve in size.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：把成本减半、把数量减半、体积缩小一半。

normal.en: Double is its opposite; split is looser because the parts may be unequal.
normal.cn: double 是它的反义；split 更宽松，因为分出的几份可以不等。

abstract.en: Picture a judge laying a ruler down the exact centre of a sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把尺子压在纸张的正中央。

abstract.en: Picture a long queue where every other person leaves at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长队，每隔一个人就同时离开，队伍立刻短了一半。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag being ripped in two, and only the smaller half kept.
abstract.cn: 想象价签被撕成两半，只留下小的那一半。

examples.en: Halve the dough and roll each piece flat.
examples.cn: 把面团分成两半，再把每块擀平。

examples.en: The new bridge has halved the time needed to cross the river.
examples.cn: 新桥把过河所需的时间缩短了一半。

examples.en: Energy use in the building halved after the windows were replaced.
examples.cn: 更换窗户后，这栋楼的能耗减了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈夫」——哈一口就剩下半个；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 healf（一半、一侧）→ 名词 half + 动词后缀 -en → 中古英语 halven → 现代英语 halve，核心义「使成一半」。

sensesIntro.en: One verb from half covers five uses: cutting into equal parts, reducing to fifty per cent, the physical cut, the self-shrinking intransitive, and the golf draw.
sensesIntro.cn: 由 half 来的这一个动词涵盖五种用法：平分、减到一半、实物对切、自身减半以及高尔夫中的平分一洞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knife going straight down the middle of one object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一刀从正中间切下，把一件东西分开。

branches.en: EQUAL SPLIT: the object becomes two parts of the same size.
branches.cn: 平分为二：整体变成大小相同的两部分。

branches.en: AMOUNT CUT: numbers, costs and time lose half their value.
branches.cn: 数量削减：数字、成本与时间失去一半。

branches.en: VISIBLE CUT: fruit, bread and planks are physically halved.
branches.cn: 可见的刀口：水果、面包、木板被真正切成两半。

branches.en: FAIR PLAY: an equal split in golf gives each player half the point.
branches.cn: 公平分配：高尔夫里平分一洞，各得一半分数。

branches.en: BOTH SIDES OF ONE CHANGE: the same halving can be said with or without an object.
branches.cn: 同一个变化的两面：同一种减半可以带宾语，也可以不带。

intro.en: Halve is a Germanic-English verb, built on half rather than on a Latin root; its family is small and transparent.
intro.cn: halve 是日耳曼语来源的英语动词，由 half 构成而非拉丁词根，词族小而透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no direct ancestor of halve; the classical word for dividing in two is dividere, and the half element is medietas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有 halve 的直接祖先；古典拉丁语表示「分成两半」的动词是 dividere，「一半」的说法是 medietas。

items.example: Half of the class was absent.
items.exampleCN: 班里有一半人缺勤。

items.example: The ending turned the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这一词尾把名词变成动词。

items.example: Let us halve the bill.
items.exampleCN: 我们把账单对半分吧。

items.meaningCN: 减少一半（第三人称单数）
items.example: The scheme halves waiting times.
items.exampleCN: 该方案把等待时间减半。

items.example: Sales halved last year.
items.exampleCN: 去年销量减半。

items.meaning: the act of cutting in two
items.example: Halving prices attracted new buyers.
items.exampleCN: 价格减半吸引了新买家。

items.example: The prefix marks doubling or splitting.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「二」或分裂。

items.example: The line bisects the angle.
items.exampleCN: 这条线平分该角。

items.example: A semicircle is a half circle.
items.exampleCN: semicircle 就是半个圆。

definition_zh: 小村庄；村落
definition_en: a very small village, usually with a few houses and no church or shop of its own
core_image: 山谷里聚在一起的几户人家，屋顶冒着小股炊烟
scene: 画家沿着乡间小路走到谷底，看见几户人家的屋顶挤在一起。The painter followed a country lane into a valley and found a little hamlet of five cottages.
sceneCN: 这里 hamlet 是「小村庄」（第 1 个义项：只有几户人家的极小村落）；句意：画家沿着乡间小路走到谷底，发现了一个只有五间农舍的小村庄。

collocations.zh: 村镇与小村落（地方行政用语）

derivatives.zh: 古词，意为「村庄；小镇」，是 hamlet 的缩短形式，今仅存于地名中
同出古英语家宅词根，与 hamlet 共享「住所」语义，并非派生

senses.title: A very small village
senses.definition: a small settlement of a few houses, smaller than a village and often without a church
senses.definitionCN: 由几户人家组成的居民点，比村庄还小，通常没有教堂
senses.example: They live in a hamlet of only six houses.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一个只有六户人家的小村庄里。
senses.why: The core image is a little heap of homes: the suffix marks something small, so a hamlet is a tiny cluster of dwellings.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一小堆家宅：词尾表示「小」，所以 hamlet 就是一小撮住所聚成的居民点。

senses.title: A rural settlement without a church
senses.definition: in British local administration, a settlement that has a name but no church of its own
senses.definitionCN: 在英国地方行政中，有名字却没有自己教堂的聚落
senses.example: The hamlet belongs to the parish of the next village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小聚落隶属于邻村的教区。
senses.why: Because hamlets were too small to raise a church, the administrative meaning grew from the size sense.
senses.whyCN: 因为小村落太小，建不起教堂，行政上的定义就从「规模小」这一层自然长出来。

senses.title: A quiet out-of-the-way place
senses.definition: any quiet, remote and closely knit little community
senses.definitionCN: 任何安静、偏远而又紧密的小社群
senses.example: The island is little more than a hamlet in the Atlantic.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛不过是大西洋上一个偏僻的小地方。
senses.why: The smallness and remoteness of real hamlets turn the word into a shorthand for a sleepy out-of-the-way place.
senses.whyCN: 真实小村落的狭小与偏远，使这个词引申为「沉睡般偏僻安静之处」的代名词。

intro.en: Hamlet comes from Old French hamelet, a double diminutive of Old French hamel, which itself comes from Late Latin hamellum, a village.
intro.cn: hamlet 来自古法语 hamelet，它是在 hamel 后叠加指小词尾 -et 而成的形式，hamel 又源自晚期拉丁语 hamellum（村庄）。

items.en: Reconstructed haimaz meant a home, a settlement.
items.cn: 重构形式 haimaz 意为「家宅、住处」。

items.en: Hām means home, and the same root gives ham, a village.
items.cn: 古英语 hām 意为「家」，同一词根还产生 ham（村庄）。

items.en: Late Latin hamellum names a small village; some scholars treat it as a borrowing from Germanic speech.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 hamellum 指小村庄；一般认为它是从日耳曼语借入的。

items.en: Hamel means a village, and hamelet is its little form.
items.cn: 古法语 hamel 意为村庄，hamelet 是它的指小形式。

items.en: Hamelet enters English meaning a small group of houses.
items.cn: hamelet 在十四世纪进入英语，意为几户房屋组成的小聚落。

items.en: The spelling settles as hamlet and also becomes the name of a famous prince.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 hamlet，同时因为莎士比亚的悲剧，也成了一个著名王子的名字。

note.en: Hamlet is a small-village word from the Germanic home root, while ham and home are its older relatives and settlement words share its meaning.
note.cn: hamlet 是源自日耳曼「家宅」词根的小村庄词，ham 与 home 是它的老近亲，而各种聚落词与它同属一个义场。

entries.definition: an old word for a village or small town, now mostly seen in place names
entries.definitionCN: 古义为村庄或小镇，如今多只见于地名，与 hamlet 同根

entries.definition: the place where a person lives
entries.definitionCN: 家；住所，与 hamlet 共用「家宅」词根

entries.definition: a dish of beaten eggs cooked in a pan
entries.definitionCN: 煎蛋卷，只是拼写结尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a settlement larger than a hamlet, often with a church
entries.definitionCN: 村庄，比 hamlet 大，通常有教堂

entries.definition: a village or district with its own local government
entries.definitionCN: 乡镇；建制镇

entries.definition: any place where people have come to live permanently
entries.definitionCN: 定居点；聚落，是 hamlet 的上位概念

normalIntro.en: Hamlet is home made small: ham plus the little ending let, a few homes gathered together.
normalIntro.cn: hamlet 就是被缩小的家：ham 加上表示「小」的结尾 let，也就是几座家宅聚在一起。

normal.en: The -let ending means little, as in booklet and droplet; so a hamlet is a little ham, a tiny village.
normal.cn: 结尾 -let 表示「小」，如 booklet（小册子）和 droplet（小水滴）；所以 hamlet 就是小小的村庄。

normal.en: Ham is an old word for a village, surviving in place names such as Birmingham.
normal.cn: ham 是「村庄」的老词，如今还留在像 Birmingham 这样的地名里。

normal.en: Compare village: a village has a church and a shop, a hamlet is smaller.
normal.cn: 对比 village：村庄有教堂有小店，hamlet 比它更小。

normal.en: A hamlet is a handful of roofs in the countryside.
normal.cn: hamlet 就是乡间寥寥几片屋顶。

normal.en: The Prince in the play is called Hamlet, but the village word came first.
normal.cn: 剧中的王子叫 Hamlet，但表示村庄的这个词出现得更早。

abstract.en: Picture five cottages huddled together at the bottom of a valley, smoke rising from each chimney.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷底五座农舍挤在一起，每根烟囱都冒着烟。

abstract.en: Think of a place so small that it has a name but no church.
abstract.cn: 想象一个地方小到只有名字、没有自己的教堂。

abstract.en: Imagine a distant island with one lane and a dozen neighbours who all know each other.
abstract.cn: 想象远方小岛上只有一条小路，十几户邻居彼此都认识。

examples.en: The hamlet lies three miles from the nearest town.
examples.cn: 这个小村庄离最近的城镇有三英里。

examples.en: Several hamlets were cut off by the snowstorm.
examples.cn: 暴风雪切断了几个小村庄的对外通道。

examples.en: Whispers spread fast through such a small hamlet.
examples.cn: 在这样的小村庄里，闲话传得飞快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈姆」加「小」：哈姆雷特住的地方就是一个小村庄；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语重构形式 haimaz（家宅）→ 古英语 hām（家）与 ham（村庄）→ 晚期拉丁语 hamellum（小村）→ 古法语 hamel / hamelet（指小）→ 中古英语 hamelet → 现代英语 hamlet，核心义「一小撮家宅聚成的居民点」。

sensesIntro.en: Hamlet begins with a handful of homes, then narrows into an administrative unit without a church, and finally widens into any quiet out-of-the-way community.
sensesIntro.cn: hamlet 从几座家宅起步，先收窄为没有教堂的行政小聚落，最后放宽为任何偏僻安静的小社群。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few houses huddled together in a valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里挤在一起的几户人家。

branches.en: The everyday sense is simply a small village.
branches.cn: 日常义项就是小村庄。

branches.en: Because it is too small for a church, it becomes an administrative label.
branches.cn: 因为小到建不起教堂，它就成了行政上的标签。

branches.en: Small and remote together produce the figurative sleepy-place sense.
branches.cn: 「小」与「偏远」合在一起，产生比喻性的「沉睡之地」义。

branches.en: Most hamlets are both tiny settlements and units without churches.
branches.cn: 多数小村落既是很小的居民点，也是没有教堂的单位。

branches.en: A real cluster of houses easily stands for any close-knit quiet place.
branches.cn: 真实的几户人家很容易代表任何紧密安静的所在。

intro.en: Hamlet is built from the old village word ham plus the diminutive ending -let, so a hamlet is literally a little ham.
intro.cn: hamlet 由古老的村庄词 ham 加上指小词尾 -let 构成，字面上就是「小小的村庄」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form hamellum is a small village, generally taken as a borrowing from Germanic speech; the true root is the Germanic home word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hamellum 意为小村庄，一般认为借自日耳曼语；真正的词根是日耳曼语的「家宅」词。

items.example: Ham survives in place names such as Nottingham.
items.exampleCN: ham 还留在 Nottingham 这类地名里。

items.example: Home and ham share one old root.
items.exampleCN: home 与 ham 共享一个古老词根。

items.example: Old French hamel passed the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 hamel 把这个词带入英语。

items.example: The ending -et turns hamel into hamelet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -et 把 hamel 变成 hamelet。

items.example: Hamlet keeps the little-village sense.
items.exampleCN: hamlet 保留「小村庄」之义。

items.example: The suffix -let also forms booklet and droplet.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -let 还构成 booklet 与 droplet。

items.example: Booklet shows the same little ending.
items.exampleCN: booklet 显示了同样的指小结尾。

items.example: Droplet is a tiny drop of water.
items.exampleCN: droplet 就是一小滴水。

items.meaning: a settlement larger than a hamlet
items.example: A village usually has a church.
items.exampleCN: 村庄通常有教堂。

definition_zh: 妨碍；阻碍；牵制；有盖的大篮子；篮中食物
definition_en: to make it difficult for someone or something to move, act or progress; also a large basket with a lid
core_image: 一只有盖的藤篮把东西扣在下面，拎起来便迈不开步
scene: 工地的运输被连绵大雨拖住了，工程负责人只好重排工期。Heavy rain continued to hamper the delivery of building materials.
sceneCN: 这里 hamper 是「妨碍」（第 1 个义项：使行动或进展变得困难）；句意：大雨持续妨碍建筑材料的运送。

pos.zh: 有盖的大篮子；篮装食物

derivatives.zh: un-（不）+ hampered（被妨碍的），意为「不受阻碍的」
动词加 -ing 构成的名词或形容词，意为「妨碍（的）」

senses.title: To hinder or slow something down
senses.definition: to make it harder for someone or something to act or make progress
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某事更难行动或取得进展
senses.example: Poor roads hamper trade in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的道路妨碍了该地区的贸易。
senses.why: The core image is something caught and pulled back, so modern use keeps the idea of being held up.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是被套住、被往回拖，因此现代用法保留了「被拖住」的感觉。

senses.title: To be held back by difficulties
senses.definition: to be held back or burdened by a problem, often used in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 被某个问题拖住或压住，常用于被动语态
senses.example: Rescue teams were hampered by thick smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 浓烟使救援队伍行动受阻。
senses.why: In the passive the verb turns the hinderer into a heavy load that keeps the subject in place.
senses.whyCN: 用于被动时，妨碍物变成了压住主语的重负，使它无法动弹。

senses.title: A large basket with a lid
senses.definition: a large basket with a lid, used for carrying food or clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带盖子的大篮子，用来装食物或衣物
senses.example: She packed a hamper for the journey to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 她为去海边的旅程装了一篮食物。
senses.why: The basket sense shows the same containment image as a concrete container you must carry.
senses.whyCN: 篮子义把同样的「容器」意象具体化为需要一提就走了的实物。

senses.title: Food packed in such a basket
senses.definition: the food and drink given in a hamper, especially as a gift or for a picnic
senses.definitionCN: 装在篮中的食品饮料，尤指作为礼物或野餐之用
senses.example: The hotel guests received a small hamper of local cheese and wine.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店客人收到了一小篮本地的奶酪和葡萄酒。
senses.why: By metonymy the container stands for the treat inside it, a pattern common with basket words.
senses.whyCN: 以容器代指其中的恩物，这是篮子类词常见的借代。

intro.en: Hamper has two separate histories that happened to share a spelling: the verb is probably an old English word meaning to shackle, and the basket is from Old French hanapier, a case for cups.
intro.cn: hamper 有两条各自独立的来源，恰好拼写相同：动词可能来自中古英语的「束缚」义，篮子义则来自古法语的酒杯箱。

items.en: The verb may be related to an old verb meaning to grasp or cramp; the origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词或许与表示「抓住、拘束」的古词有关，来源不确定。

items.en: Hamperen appears meaning to entangle or hold back.
items.cn: 约十四世纪出现 hamperen，意为缠住、拖住。

items.en: Hanapier names a case for hanaps, old beakers or cups.
items.cn: 古法语 hanapier 指装酒罐（hanap）的箱子。

items.en: A hamper becomes a large covered basket carried on the road.
items.cn: hamper 成为旅途中提着的带盖大篮子。

items.en: Hampers of food are sent as gifts, and the verb settles as hinder.
items.cn: 装食品的篮子常作礼物相送，动词义则稳定为「妨碍」。

note.en: The verb hamper is close to hinder and impede, while the basket sense belongs to a different group of container words.
note.cn: 动词 hamper 与 hinder、impede 接近，篮子义则属于另一组容器词，两义各走一路。

entries.definition: the third-person form of the verb, or the plural of the basket noun
entries.definitionCN: 动词三单或篮子名词复数，是 hamper 的屈折形式

entries.definition: held back or slowed
entries.definitionCN: 受阻碍的，是 hamper 的过去分词

entries.definition: a tool for hitting nails
entries.definitionCN: 锤子，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make it difficult for something to happen
entries.definitionCN: 妨碍；阻碍，与 hamper 最接近

entries.definition: to delay or block progress
entries.definitionCN: 阻碍；阻挠，较正式

entries.definition: to block a road, passage or process
entries.definitionCN: 阻塞；阻挡

entries.definition: a container made of woven material
entries.definitionCN: 篮子，是 hamper 篮子义的上位词

normalIntro.en: Hamper carries a rope image in the verb and a basket image in the noun, so tie the two together.
normalIntro.cn: hamper 的动词义像一根绳子，名词义像一只篮子，把两者绑在一起记最稳。

normal.en: Hamper is often used with progress, efforts, growth and recovery.
normal.cn: hamper 常与 progress、efforts、growth、recovery 搭配，表示拖慢这些进程。

normal.en: The passive form be hampered by is very common in reports.
normal.cn: 被动结构 be hampered by 在新闻报道中极其常见。

normal.en: A picnic hamper is a basket of food carried on a trip.
normal.cn: a picnic hamper 就是旅途上拎着的一篮食物。

normal.en: Do not confuse hamper with hammer: the basket has no nails.
normal.cn: 不要把 hamper 和 hammer 搞混：篮子并不钉钉子。

normal.en: Unhampered adds un- and means free from any hindrance.
normal.cn: unhampered 加前缀 un-，表示「不受任何阻碍」。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner whose shoelaces are tied together by a bystander.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者被旁人把两根鞋带系在了一起。

abstract.en: Picture a cart with one jammed wheel dragging along a road.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车有一只轮子卡住了，沿路被拖着走。

abstract.en: Think of a big lidded basket too heavy to lift quickly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只有盖的大篮子，沉得一下子提不起来。

examples.en: Lack of funding has hampered the research project.
examples.cn: 资金不足妨碍了这个研究项目。

examples.en: The search was hampered by heavy snow and poor visibility.
examples.cn: 大雪和能见度差使搜寻行动受阻。

examples.en: They carried a hamper of sandwiches to the beach.
examples.cn: 他们提着一篮三明治去了海滩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「憨怕」——一筐东西太沉拎不动，只能憨憨地怕着慢慢挪；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 动词义可能来自中古英语的束缚类词（来源不确定）；篮子义来自古法语 hanapier（酒杯箱）→ 英语 hamper；两条来源拼写重合，现代英语中并行发展，核心义「拖住、装住」。

sensesIntro.en: Hamper runs two tracks: a verb track of holding someone back, and a noun track of a big lidded basket and the food in it.
sensesIntro.cn: hamper 有两条线：一条动词线表示把人拖住，一条名词线表示带盖大篮子及篮里的食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lidded basket that pins things down so they cannot move freely.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带盖的篮子把东西压在下面，使其动弹不得。

branches.en: The main verb sense is to hinder or slow progress.
branches.cn: 动词主义是妨碍或拖慢进展。

branches.en: The passive sense shows something pinned in place by a problem.
branches.cn: 被动义表现被问题钉在原地的状态。

branches.en: The concrete object sense is a large basket with a lid.
branches.cn: 具体实物义是带盖的大篮子。

branches.en: The food sense borrows the container to name its contents.
branches.cn: 食物义借容器之名代指其中内容。

branches.en: Both a hinderer and a burden keep the subject from moving forward.
branches.cn: 阻碍者与重负都让主语无法前进。

intro.en: Hamper is not built from productive English pieces; its two senses come from separate sources that merged in spelling.
intro.cn: hamper 并非由英语构词成分拼成，它的两个义项来自两条不同的来源，只是拼写合流。

latinIntro.en: No direct Latin root is proven; the basket sense traces to Old French hanapier, and the verb origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁语词根；篮子义可溯至古法语 hanapier，动词来源不确定。

items.meaning: a case for beakers or cups
items.example: Hanapier is the source of the basket sense.
items.exampleCN: hanapier 是篮子义项的来源。

items.example: Traffic can hamper a whole morning.
items.exampleCN: 交通堵塞可能妨碍一整个上午。

items.example: The noun names a basket of food.
items.exampleCN: 名词义指一篮食物。

items.example: The ending -ed forms hampered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 hampered。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unhampered.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unhampered。

items.example: Unhampered growth needs steady demand.
items.exampleCN: 不受阻碍的增长需要稳定的需求。

items.example: Hinder is the closest everyday verb.
items.exampleCN: hinder 是最近的日常近义动词。

items.example: Impede is more formal than hamper.
items.exampleCN: impede 比 hamper 更正式。

definition_zh: 仓鼠
definition_en: a small furry animal with short ears, a short tail and big cheek pouches, often kept as a pet
core_image: 一只小鼠把葵花籽塞进鼓鼓的颊囊，跑进转轮
scene: 同桌说家里养了一只灰色的小动物，每天夜里都在笼子里跑轮子。My classmate keeps a hamster in a cage beside her bed.
sceneCN: 这里 hamster 是「仓鼠」（第 1 个义项：常被当宠物饲养的小型啮齿动物）；句意：我的同桌在床边笼子里养了一只仓鼠。

collocations.zh: 像仓鼠跑轮一样原地打转的经济

derivatives.zh: hamster 加 -like（像……一样的），意为「像仓鼠的」
由 hamster 加 -ing 构成的新造词，指「像仓鼠一样囤积」，多用于网络语境

senses.title: The small pet rodent
senses.definition: a small furry rodent kept as a pet, busy at night and fond of storing food
senses.definitionCN: 一种被当宠物饲养的小型毛茸茸啮齿动物，夜间活跃，喜欢囤食
senses.example: Our hamster sleeps all day and runs at night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的仓鼠白天睡觉，夜里跑轮子。
senses.why: From the German name for a hoarding grain-eater, English first knew the hamster as this little food-storing animal.
senses.whyCN: 由德语中「囤粮的吃谷者」之名而来，英语最先认识的就是这种会存粮的小动物。

senses.title: The species in the wild
senses.definition: one of several wild species of the genus Cricetus and its relatives, living in underground burrows
senses.definitionCN: 仓鼠属及其近缘属的若干野生物种，住在地洞里
senses.example: European hamsters build deep burrows in farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 欧洲仓鼠在农田里挖深深的地洞。
senses.why: The same name covers the wild relatives, whose burrows and cheek pouches show the storing habit in nature.
senses.whyCN: 同一名称也覆盖野生近亲，它们的地洞与颊囊在自然界中同样体现囤食习性。

senses.title: A figure of pointless repetitive effort
senses.definition: a metaphor for busy, repetitive activity that goes nowhere, as in running on a hamster wheel
senses.definitionCN: 比喻忙忙碌碌却原地踏步的活动，源自仓鼠跑轮
senses.example: Many workers feel stuck on a hamster wheel of rent and bills.
senses.exampleCN: 许多工人觉得自己被困在房租和账单的跑轮上。
senses.why: Because a hamster spins a wheel without moving forward, the word pictures effort with no progress.
senses.whyCN: 因为仓鼠在轮子里跑得飞快却原地不动，这个词就用来描摹「努力而无进展」。

intro.en: Hamster is borrowed from German Hamster, which goes back to an Old High German name for a grain-earer; the modern animal sense is attested in English from the 1600s.
intro.cn: hamster 借自德语 Hamster，可上溯到古高地德语中意为「吃谷穗者」的名称；现代动物义在英语中约十七世纪已有记录。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hamstra- is generally linked to an old word for stinking or pungent.
items.cn: 一般认为重构形式如 hamstra- 与表示「发臭、有异味」的古词有关。

items.en: Hamustro names the animal; folk etymology later reads it as eater of ears of corn.
items.cn: 古高地德语 hamustro 指这种动物；后来民间把它理解为「吃谷穗者」。

items.en: Modern German Hamster keeps the animal name.
items.cn: 现代德语 Hamster 保留了动物名。

items.en: English borrows hamster for the corn-storing rodent of Germany.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 hamster，指德国那种囤玉米的啮齿动物。

items.en: After the 1930s hamster becomes a familiar pet and a figure for pointless spinning.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代以后，仓鼠成为常见宠物，也成了「空转」的比喻。

note.en: Hamster is a borrowed German animal name; it sits among other small pet rodents and is easy to confuse with its near relatives.
note.cn: hamster 是借自德语的动物名，与其它小型宠物啮齿动物相邻，也容易和近亲混淆。

entries.definition: the past form of a rare verb meaning to store like a hamster
entries.definitionCN: 稀有动词的过去式，意为像仓鼠一样囤积

entries.definition: resembling a hamster
entries.definitionCN: 像仓鼠一样的

entries.definition: a common misspelling with an extra p
entries.definitionCN: 多写一个 p 的常见错拼，正确拼写没有 p

entries.definition: a small furry rodent often kept as a pet
entries.definitionCN: 豚鼠；天竺鼠，常见宠物啮齿动物

entries.definition: a small desert rodent with a long tail
entries.definitionCN: 沙鼠，尾巴长的小型宠物啮齿动物

entries.definition: a small rodent with a long thin tail
entries.definitionCN: 老鼠；小鼠

normalIntro.en: Hamster is a borrowed German animal name, so learn it as a pet word and hook it to a wheel and a cage.
normalIntro.cn: hamster 是借来的德语动物名，可当作宠物词来记，把它和转轮、笼子挂钩。

normal.en: A hamster wheel is the picture of effort without progress.
normal.cn: hamster wheel（仓鼠跑轮）是「努力却无进展」的典型画面。

normal.en: Hamsters carry food in their cheeks, which is why they look so puffed up.
normal.cn: 仓鼠把食物塞在颊囊里，所以看起来总是鼓鼓的。

normal.en: Compare gerbil and guinea pig: these are the neighbours in the pet shop.
normal.cn: 对比 gerbil 和 guinea pig：它们是宠物店里相邻的名字。

normal.en: Remember the spelling has no p in the middle, unlike hampster.
normal.cn: 记住拼写中间没有 p，不要写成 hampster。

normal.en: Hamster economics is a sarcastic phrase for a life spent spinning.
normal.cn: hamster economics 是讽刺「一辈子在轮子里打转」的说法。

abstract.en: Picture two round cheeks stuffed with seeds like two tiny sacks.
abstract.cn: 想象两侧圆鼓鼓的颊囊，像两个塞满种子的小口袋。

abstract.en: Imagine a wheel creaking night after night while the animal stays in the same spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一只轮子夜夜吱呀作响，而小动物始终停在原地。

abstract.en: Think of a tiny guard hoarding grain deep under a field.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小小的守卫在田野深处囤积谷物。

examples.en: She fed her hamster a piece of carrot.
examples.cn: 她给仓鼠喂了一小片胡萝卜。

examples.en: Hamsters are nocturnal, so they are most active after dark.
examples.cn: 仓鼠是夜行动物，所以天黑后最活跃。

examples.en: He complained that his job felt like running on a hamster wheel.
examples.cn: 他抱怨自己的工作就像在仓鼠跑轮上奔跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「憨姆斯特」——一只憨憨的小家伙抱着坚果在轮子里转；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构的日耳曼语形式（一般认为与「发臭」义有关）→ 古高地德语 hamustro（这种动物，后被民间理解为「吃谷穗者」）→ 德语 Hamster → 英语 hamster，核心义「囤粮的小型啮齿动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Hamster starts as a borrowed animal name, extends to its wild relatives, and then turns into a metaphor for endless spinning.
sensesIntro.cn: hamster 从借入的动物名起步，扩展到它的野生近亲，再转化为「无休止空转」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small rodent stuffing seeds into its cheeks before it runs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小鼠把种子塞进颊囊，然后飞奔。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the little pet rodent.
branches.cn: 日常义就是这只宠物小啮齿动物。

branches.en: The wild species sense names the burrow-dwelling relatives.
branches.cn: 野生义指住在地洞里的近亲物种。

branches.en: The wheel turns the animal into a picture of pointless effort.
branches.cn: 跑轮使这只动物变成「白费力气」的图景。

branches.en: Pet and wild hamsters share the cheek pouches and the storing habit.
branches.cn: 宠物仓鼠与野生仓鼠共享颊囊和囤食习性。

branches.en: A pet running its wheel supplies the metaphor of spinning without progress.
branches.cn: 宠物跑轮的画面直接提供了「空转不出进展」的比喻。

intro.en: Hamster has no transparent English pieces; it is a whole borrowed name, with only a few modern add-ons such as -like.
intro.cn: hamster 没有可拆的英语成分，它是一个完整的借词名，只有像 -like 这样少数的现代附加成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root for the common word; the scientific Latin name Cricetus is a separate coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 这个常用词没有拉丁语词根；科学拉丁语名 Cricetus 是另外造出的名称。

items.example: Hamustro is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: hamustro 是最早有记录的形式。

items.example: German kept the name as Hamster.
items.exampleCN: 德语把这个名字保留为 Hamster。

items.example: English borrowed hamster in the 1600s.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪借入了 hamster。

items.example: The suffix -like forms hamsterlike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 hamsterlike。

items.meaning: a running wheel for a pet rodent
items.example: The compound hamster wheel names the toy.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 hamster wheel 指这种玩具轮。

items.meaning: a cage for keeping a hamster
items.example: The compound hamster cage names the home.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 hamster cage 指它的住处。

items.example: Cricetus is the genus name of typical hamsters.
items.exampleCN: Cricetus 是典型仓鼠的属名。

items.example: A hamster is a small rodent.
items.exampleCN: 仓鼠是一种小型啮齿动物。

items.example: Hamsters are nocturnal animals.
items.exampleCN: 仓鼠是夜行动物。

definition_zh: 妨碍；障碍；不利条件；残疾；让步（比赛用语）
definition_en: something that makes success harder, or the act of making it harder for someone to succeed
core_image: 赛马时往快马背上多压一只沙袋，让它和对手跑得一样费劲
scene: 两位水平相当的选手比赛，弱者先跑一段以拉平差距。Even strong runners accept a handicap when it keeps the contest close.
sceneCN: 这里 handicap 是「让步」（第 4 个义项：为求公平而给强者增加难度、给弱者优待）；句意：在公平的比赛中，较强的一方会先让较弱的一方几步作为让步。

collocations.zh: 智力障碍（旧式说法，今多用 intellectual disability）

derivatives.zh: 有残疾的；处于不利地位的；由 handicap 加过去分词后缀 -ed 构成
赛马中确定让磅条件的做法；由 handicap 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成
赛马中评定让磅条件的人；由 handicap 加表示「做某事者」的后缀 -er 构成

senses.title: Something that holds you back
senses.definition: a condition or circumstance that makes it harder for someone to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 使人更难成功的条件或处境
senses.example: A poor internet connection was a real handicap to her studies.
senses.exampleCN: 网络连接差是她学习上真正的障碍。
senses.why: The original handicap was extra weight carried by a faster horse, so any burden that slows a person down became a handicap.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 handicap 是给快马额外加的负重，于是任何拖慢人的负担都被称作 handicap，这是「负重」意象最直接的引申。

senses.title: A physical or mental disability
senses.definition: a disability that limits a person in some activity, a use now often felt to be old-fashioned
senses.definitionCN: 限制某人从事某项活动的残疾，如今这种用法常被认为过时
senses.example: Her hearing handicap made it hard to follow lectures.
senses.exampleCN: 她的听力障碍让她很难跟上讲座。
senses.why: The extra weight a horse must carry is a lasting burden, so a lasting bodily limitation was also named a handicap.
senses.whyCN: 马背上额外的重量是长期背负的，因此长期存在的身体局限也被叫作 handicap；当代多改用 disability 或 impairment。

senses.title: To make a task harder
senses.definition: to make it more difficult for someone to do something or to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更难做某事或更难成功
senses.example: High fees handicap poorer students in choosing a university.
senses.exampleCN: 高额学费使家境较差的学生在选择大学时处于不利地位。
senses.why: If assigning extra weight handicaps a horse, then any action that adds difficulty handicaps a person.
senses.whyCN: 既然给马加负重就是 handicap 它，那么任何增加难度的做法也就是在妨碍人。

senses.title: An advantage given for fairness
senses.definition: a weight, distance, or other advantage given so that competitors of different ability can contend fairly
senses.definitionCN: 为了使水平不同的选手公平竞争而给予的重量、距离或其他优待
senses.example: In the golf match the top players played off a handicap.
senses.exampleCN: 在高尔夫球赛中，高手们按让杆数出场。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the official weigh-in settled the extra weight that evened the contest.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：正式称重决定了用于拉平差距的额外重量，负重反而变成了公平的保证。

senses.title: A disadvantage that comes first
senses.definition: a disadvantage built into the starting position of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体在起始位置上就带有的劣势
senses.example: Children raised in poverty start life with a handicap.
senses.exampleCN: 在贫困中长大的孩子一出生就背负着劣势。
senses.why: A handicap is fixed before the race begins, so anything fixed before someone starts life works the same way.
senses.whyCN: handicap 在比赛开始前就已定好，因此人生起跑前就固定下来的劣势也用同一个词。

intro.en: Handicap comes from an old gambling game in which money was put into a cap, and from the phrase hand in cap.
intro.cn: handicap 来自一种古老的赌博游戏：钱被放进帽子里抽签互换，源于短语 hand in cap（手放在帽子里）。

items.en: The phrase hand in cap named a game of drawing from a cap to exchange goods with payment.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语短语 hand in cap 指伸手入帽抽签、以付款换物品的游戏。

items.en: Handicap became a horse race in which weights were assigned to even the chances.
items.cn: handicap 成为赛马术语，赛事会分配负重以拉平各马的获胜机会。

items.en: The word spread to golf, cycling, and other sports as a word for an equalising allowance.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到高尔夫、自行车等运动，指用于拉平差距的让步。

items.en: The verb handicaps appears, meaning to put someone at a disadvantage.
items.cn: 动词 forms handicaps 出现，意为使某人处于不利地位。

items.en: The noun came to mean any disability or drawback, and modern usage often prefers disability.
items.cn: 名词引申为任何残疾或不利条件，现代用法多改用 disability。

items.en: Today handicap is common in sport, in statistics, and in figurative talk of burdens.
items.cn: 今天 handicap 常见于体育、统计以及对负担的比喻说法中。

note.en: Handicap is close to hand and to the idea of an extra burden, and to words for disadvantage and disability.
note.cn: handicap 与 hand 以及「负重」的意象相邻，也与表示劣势和残疾的词相邻。

entries.definition: the part of the body at the end of the arm
entries.definitionCN: 手；handicap 拼写里含有 hand，但词义与手无关

entries.definition: a small number or amount
entries.definitionCN: 一把；少量

entries.definition: having a disability or disadvantage
entries.definitionCN: 有残疾的；处于不利地位的

entries.definition: an unfavourable condition
entries.definitionCN: 不利条件；劣势

entries.definition: something that blocks progress
entries.definitionCN: 障碍；阻碍

entries.definition: a condition that limits a person in some activity
entries.definitionCN: 残疾；无能力；这一说法较 handicap 更中性，值得优先使用

normalIntro.en: Handicap began as a cap full of money and turned into a bag of weights that evened a race.
normalIntro.cn: handicap 最早是一只装着钱的帽子，后来变成让赛马公平的一袋配重。

normal.en: Recall hand in cap, the old game that gave the word its start.
normal.cn: 回想短语「hand in cap」，这个古老的游戏正是这个词的来源。

normal.en: In sport a handicap gives a weaker player a head start.
normal.cn: 在体育中，handicap 给较弱的一方先行一步的优势。

normal.en: The verb handicap pairs with money, rules, and conditions.
normal.cn: 动词 handicap 常与金钱、规则、条件搭配，表示这些因素让人吃亏。

normal.en: Be handicapped by is the common passive phrase.
normal.cn: 「be handicapped by」是最常见的被动搭配。

normal.en: In careful modern English, say person with a disability instead of handicap.
normal.cn: 在严谨的现代表达中，应说 a person with a disability，而不用 handicap 指人。

abstract.en: Picture a strong horse carrying a bag of sand so a weak horse keeps up.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹强壮的马背着沙袋，好让弱马跟得上。

abstract.en: Imagine a leader giving the other side a generous head start.
abstract.cn: 想象领先者主动让对手先跑一段，以显示公平。

abstract.en: Think of a heavy bag tied to a runner at the starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条沉重的口袋在起跑线前绑在跑者身上。

examples.en: Not speaking the local language was a serious handicap for the newcomers.
examples.cn: 不会说当地语言对新来的人来说是一个严重的障碍。

examples.en: The old rules handicapped small firms unfairly.
examples.cn: 旧规则使小公司不公平地处于不利地位。

examples.en: The race used a handicap system so that every boat had a fair chance.
examples.cn: 这场比赛采用让分制度，好让每条船都有公平的机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「汉迪卡普」——把「汉」子的「迪」斯科卡在「普」通人身上，就成了拖后腿的障碍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语短语 hand in cap（手放在帽子里，一种十七世纪的抽签换物游戏）→ handicap（赛马让磅制度）→ 泛指障碍、残疾、妨碍，核心义「额外负重」。

sensesIntro.en: Handicap first named an official weight or allowance, then any burden, then a disability, and finally the act of putting someone at a disadvantage.
sensesIntro.cn: handicap 先指官方指定的负重或让步，再泛指负担、残疾，最后指使人处于不利地位的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag of extra weight tied to a fast horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：绑在快马背上的额外负重。

branches.en: Any burden that slows progress is a generalised handicap.
branches.cn: 任何拖慢进展的负担都是泛化后的 handicap。

branches.en: A lasting bodily limit was once called a handicap.
branches.cn: 长期的身体局限曾被称作 handicap，如今多用 disability。

branches.en: The verb names the act of adding weight or difficulty.
branches.cn: 动词义指加重负担、增加难度的动作。

branches.en: The racing sense survives as the source of all the others.
branches.cn: 赛马义项作为其余义项的源头仍在使用。

branches.en: All three senses concern something that is added or fixed in advance and works against someone.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都涉及事先加上或固定下来的、对某人不利的东西。

intro.en: Handicap began as an English phrase, not a Latin root, and English built handicapped, handicapper, and handicapping around it.
intro.cn: handicap 最初是英语中的短语而非拉丁词根，英语围绕它构成 handicapped、handicapper 与 handicapping。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source word for handicap; the phrase hand in cap is native English.
latinIntro.cn: handicap 没有拉丁语源词，其来源是土生英语短语 hand in cap。

items.meaning: the hand, as in hand in cap
items.meaningCN: 手；出现在 hand in cap 中，与词义无直接关系
items.example: The hand in the story is simply reaching into a cap.
items.exampleCN: 故事里的手只是伸进帽子里罢了。

items.meaning: a cap, the container in the old game
items.meaningCN: 帽子；指旧游戏中装钱的容器
items.example: Money for the draw was held in a cap.
items.exampleCN: 抽签用的钱放在一顶帽子里。

items.meaning: a draw game using a cap
items.example: Hand in cap named an exchange game.
items.exampleCN: hand in cap 是一种以货易货的游戏。

items.example: Handicap first named a race condition.
items.exampleCN: handicap 最初指赛马条件。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms the adjective handicapped.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成形容词 handicapped。

items.meaningCN: 有残疾的；处于不利地位的
items.example: Handicapped has largely given way to other terms.
items.exampleCN: handicapped 已多被其他说法取代。

items.meaningCN: 表示从事某事者的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms handicapper.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 handicapper。

items.meaning: a person who sets the handicap
items.example: The handicapper gave each horse its weight.
items.exampleCN: 让磅员为每匹马评定了负重。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms handicapping.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 handicapping。

items.example: Handicapping keeps a race competitive.
items.exampleCN: 评定让磅能让比赛保持竞争性。

definition_zh: （发给听者的）讲义；传单；散发的宣传品；施舍物；政府补贴
definition_en: a sheet or paper given to students or listeners, or something given free, especially money or aid
core_image: 一只手把一叠纸或一份东西递到别人手里
scene: 老师在每节课开始时把一张写满要点的一页纸递给每一位学生。At the start of each lecture the teacher gave everyone a handout with the key points.
sceneCN: 这里 handout 是「讲义」（第 1 个义项：发给学生或听众的一页纸）；句意：每节课开始时，老师发给每人一张印有要点的讲义。

derivatives.zh: 分发；散发；由 hand 加副词 out 组成的短语动词，是 handout 的动词来源
单页讲义；由 handout 加 sheet 构成的复合名词
移交；交接；同样由 hand 加方位副词构成的短语动词，与 handout 结构相近

senses.title: A sheet given to students or listeners
senses.definition: a printed sheet of notes, exercises, or slides given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 发给听众的讲稿、练习或幻灯片打印页
senses.example: The tutor put the diagrams on a handout so we could follow along.
senses.exampleCN: 导师把图表放在讲义上，好让我们边听边看。
senses.why: The compound is hand plus out, so a sheet that is handed out to each person is a handout.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 hand 与 out 组合而成，被逐份分发出去的纸自然就叫 handout，即「递出去的东西」。

senses.title: A leaflet or flyer
senses.definition: a printed advertisement or information sheet given to people in the street
senses.definitionCN: 在街头发给行人的宣传或信息印刷品
senses.example: Volunteers gave out a handout about the beach clean-up.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者发放了一份海滩清理活动的宣传单。
senses.why: Leaflets are literally handed out on the street, so the same compound names them.
senses.whyCN: 传单就是在街头被「递出去」的，因此同一组词也用来指它，强调面对面派发。

senses.title: A gift of food or money
senses.definition: money, food, or clothing given free to someone in need
senses.definitionCN: 免费给予穷困者的钱、食物或衣物
senses.example: He refused to depend on handouts from strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 他不愿靠陌生人的施舍过活。
senses.why: Anything placed into an open hand free of charge is a handout, and the word often carries a hint of charity.
senses.whyCN: 任何白送进手心的东西都是 handout，这个词常带有「慈善」甚至「白拿」的意味。

senses.title: Government aid or a subsidy
senses.definition: financial help given by a government or an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或机构发放的资金帮助
senses.example: Critics said the company was surviving on state handouts.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这家公司靠国家补贴勉强维持。
senses.why: From food and coins given to the poor to cheques from a government, the giving-from-hand image stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 从施舍给穷人的食物硬币，到政府开出的支票，递出东西这一意象始终没变，只是给予者换了。

senses.title: Something given away cheaply
senses.titleCN: 免费赠送的小册子或小样
senses.definition: an information item or small gift offered free, often to promote something
senses.definitionCN: 常为推销而免费提供的信息小册或小礼品
senses.example: The museum shop has handouts for children at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆商店在门口备有给孩子的免费小册子。
senses.why: A promo item is handed out rather than sold, so marketing expanded the sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 推销品是被发出去的而不是卖出去的，营销场景让这个词又多了一层「赠品」的含义。

intro.en: Handout is a native English compound of hand and out, modelled on the phrase verb hand out.
intro.cn: handout 是土生英语复合词，由 hand 与副词 out 组成，与短语动词 hand out 同源同构。

items.en: Hand comes from the Old English word for the hand.
items.cn: hand 来自古英语中表示「手」的词。

items.en: Out comes from the Old English word for outward, from a house or boundary.
items.cn: out 来自古英语中表示「向外」的词。

items.en: The phrase hand out became common, meaning to distribute to people.
items.cn: 短语 hand out 流行起来，意为向人分发。

items.en: The noun handout first meant a free gift or a charitable gratuity.
items.cn: 名词 handout 最初指白送的东西或慈善小费。

items.en: Handout extends to printed sheets, leaflets, and government grants.
items.cn: handout 扩展到打印讲义、传单与政府补贴。

items.en: In classrooms a handout is chiefly a study sheet, while in public life it can still mean aid.
items.cn: 在教室里 handout 主要指学习材料，在公共事务中则仍可指资助。

note.en: Handout belongs to the hand family and is close to words for printed sheets and for free gifts.
note.cn: handout 属于 hand 同族词，并与表示印刷材料和免费赠予的词相邻。

entries.definition: to give something to each person
entries.definitionCN: 分发；这是 handout 的动词形式

entries.definition: the act of giving control to someone else
entries.definitionCN: 移交；同样由 hand 加方位副词构成，义为交出控制权

entries.definition: a small quantity held in the hand
entries.definitionCN: 一把；少量

entries.definition: a small printed sheet given to people
entries.definitionCN: 小册子；传单

entries.definition: a thin book with pictures and information
entries.definitionCN: 宣传册；小册子

entries.definition: money paid by a government to support something
entries.definitionCN: 补贴；津贴；多用于政府资助的正式说法

normalIntro.en: Handout is a hand held out with papers or coins; think of the hand and the direction out.
normalIntro.cn: handout 就是一只伸出递东西的手；抓住 hand（手）与 out（向外）两个部分。

normal.en: The verb behind the noun is the phrasal hand out, to distribute to each person.
normal.cn: 名词背后的动词是短语动词 hand out，意为逐份分发。

normal.en: A course handout is a study sheet, not a charitable gift.
normal.cn: course handout 是学习材料，不是慈善赠品。

normal.en: Handout often implies getting something free, so it can sound slightly critical.
normal.cn: handout 常暗示白拿，因此可能带一点批评意味。

normal.en: For charitable money, subsidy or welfare is the more neutral word.
normal.cn: 指慈善或福利资金时，subsidy、welfare 是更中性的说法。

normal.en: Handouts is simply the plural, and handout sheet means a single page.
normal.cn: handouts 只是复数形式，handout sheet 则指单页材料。

abstract.en: See a teacher walking down the rows with a stack of pages.
abstract.cn: 想象老师抱着一叠纸沿着座位一行行发下去。

abstract.en: Picture a volunteer pressing a paper into every passer-by palm.
abstract.cn: 想象志愿者把一张纸塞进每个路人的手心。

abstract.en: Think of a coin dropped into a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币落进一只等待的手掌。

examples.en: The teacher handed out a summary of the lecture before the break.
examples.cn: 老师在课间前发了一份讲座摘要。

examples.en: Farmers should not be forced to survive on handouts, the report argues.
examples.cn: 这篇文章主张农民不应被迫靠补贴过活。

examples.en: She kept her handouts in a folder labelled by week.
examples.cn: 她把讲义按周放进文件夹里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「汉道特」——「汉」子走在「道」上特意把材料递给路人，就是分发讲义；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 hand（手）+ out（向外）→ 短语动词 hand out（分发）→ 名词 handout（分发出去的东西），核心义「伸手递出去的一份东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Handout moves from a sheet of papers distributed to students, through leaflets and charity gifts, to money granted by governments.
sensesIntro.cn: handout 从发给学生的纸页，延伸至传单、慈善施舍，最后指政府拨付的资金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stretched out holding a sheet of paper or some coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸出去，手里握着纸页或几枚硬币。

branches.en: A classroom sheet is the most common modern sense.
branches.cn: 课堂讲义是今天最常见的义项。

branches.en: A leaflet is just the same sheet handed to strangers.
branches.cn: 传单不过是递到陌生人手里的同一种纸页。

branches.en: Charity turns the page into food or coins for the poor.
branches.cn: 慈善把纸页换成了给穷人的食物或硬币。

branches.en: Organised aid makes the giver an institution.
branches.cn: 制度化援助让递出东西的人变成了机构。

branches.en: All involve something given free, which is why the word can imply dependence.
branches.cn: 这些义项都涉及免费给予，因此这个词可能暗含依赖意味。

intro.en: Handout is English hand plus the adverb out, with handout sheet and the phrasal hand out built from it.
intro.cn: handout 由英语 hand 加副词 out 构成，handout sheet 与短语动词 hand out 都由此而来。

latinIntro.en: Handout has no Latin source because it was formed inside English from two native words.
latinIntro.cn: handout 没有拉丁语来源，它由两个土生英语词在英语内部组合而成。

items.example: Hand is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: hand 是这个复合词的第一个部分。

items.example: Out supplies the outward direction.
items.exampleCN: out 提供向外的方向感。

items.meaning: to give something to each person
items.example: Volunteers hand out drinks at the finish line.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者在终点线分发饮料。

items.meaning: a sheet or gift given out
items.example: Handout names whatever is passed to people.
items.exampleCN: handout 指任何被递到人们手里的东西。

items.meaning: a single printed page for listeners
items.example: She printed the handout sheet two-sided.
items.exampleCN: 她把单页讲义印成了双面。

items.example: Hand over uses the same pattern with over.
items.exampleCN: hand over 用同样的结构加上了 over。

items.example: Handover shows the same noun pattern.
items.exampleCN: handover 体现了同一种名词构词方式。

items.example: The suffix -s forms handouts.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 handouts。

items.example: Copies of the handouts were stacked by the door.
items.exampleCN: 多份讲义堆在门旁。

items.meaning: as much as one hand holds
items.example: Handful shows hand with a quantity suffix.
items.exampleCN: handful 体现了 hand 加数量词尾的构词。

definition_zh: （电话的）听筒；（无线电话、手机）手持式设备
definition_en: the part of a telephone that is held in the hand, or a small wireless device for sending and receiving calls
core_image: 一只手握着听筒，把它凑到耳边说话
scene: 电话铃响了，会议室里的人伸手拿起听筒，示意大家安静。When the phone rang, she picked up the handset and signalled for silence.
sceneCN: 这里 handset 是「听筒」（第 1 个义项：电话上可手持、贴耳通话的部分）；句意：电话响时，她拿起听筒并示意大家安静。

derivatives.zh: 手机制造商；由 handset 加 maker（制造者）构成的复合名词
头戴式耳机、麦克风组合；同样由 head 加 set 构成的平行复合词
手持的；hand 加过去分词 held 构成，与 handset 的「手持」意象相通

senses.title: The part of a telephone held to the ear
senses.definition: the earpiece and mouthpiece of a telephone that is held in the hand while talking
senses.definitionCN: 电话上贴耳与对嘴、通话时手持的部分
senses.example: She lifted the handset from its cradle.
senses.exampleCN: 她把听筒从底座上拿起来。
senses.why: A set made to be held by the hand is literally a handset, so the movable part of a telephone took the name.
senses.whyCN: 原本指「供手拿的一套装置」，于是电话上可移动的听筒部分就被叫作 handset。

senses.title: A wireless telephone itself
senses.definition: a small wireless telephone or cordless phone that can be carried about
senses.definitionCN: 可随身携带的小型无线电话或无绳电话
senses.example: A whole new wave of handsets hit the shops that autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年出货数百万部手机。
senses.why: As phones shrank into a single held unit, the earpiece name spread to the whole device.
senses.whyCN: 电话缩小为一件手持整机后，原本指听筒的名字就扩展到了整部手机。

senses.title: A hand-held remote device
senses.definition: a small hand-held control unit for equipment such as a radio, camera, or game console
senses.definitionCN: 控制无线电、相机或游戏机等设备的小型手持部件
senses.example: The microphone comes with a separate handset for tuning stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这台收音机配有一个单独的手持件用来调台。
senses.why: The general pattern of a held set for controlling a machine extends the word beyond telephones.
senses.whyCN: 「供手拿、操控机器的一套装置」这一通用构词模式，让这个词走出电话的领域。

intro.en: Handset is an English compound of hand and set, formed in the age of the telephone.
intro.cn: handset 是英语复合词，由 hand 与 set 组成，形成于电话普及的年代。

items.en: Hand comes from the Old English word for the hand.
items.cn: hand 来自古英语表示「手」的词。

items.en: Set comes through Old French from Latin and came to mean a set of matched things.
items.cn: set 经古法语来自拉丁语，后来在英语中意为「一套、一组」。

items.en: Telephones arrived with a separate set held in the hand for talking.
items.cn: 电话出现时，通话用的是一套单独拿在手里的装置。

items.en: Handset is recorded for the earpiece and mouthpiece of a telephone.
items.cn: handset 开始被记录为电话的听筒与送话器。

items.en: Cordless and mobile phones made the handset name cover the whole device.
items.cn: 无绳电话与移动电话让 handset 泛指整部手机。

items.en: Media use handset for phones generally, especially in Asian markets, while speakers keep it for the earpiece elsewhere.
items.cn: 媒体常用 handset 泛指手机，尤其在亚洲市场；其他地区则仍用它指听筒。

note.en: Handset is close to its sibling compounds with head and ear, and to words for phones and earpieces.
note.cn: handset 与由 head、ear 构成的平行复合词相邻，也与表示电话与听筒的词相邻。

entries.definition: earphones with a microphone worn on the head
entries.definitionCN: 头戴式耳机与麦克风组合；与 handset 结构相同，只换了第一个词

entries.definition: a small telephone unit worn over the ear
entries.definitionCN: 挂在耳上的小型通话装置；使用较少

entries.definition: convenient or easy to use
entries.definitionCN: 方便的；在部分欧洲语言中借作「手机」的意思

entries.definition: the part of a telephone that receives sound
entries.definitionCN: 听筒；受话器；较 handset 更技术化

entries.definition: a telephone that works by radio signals
entries.definitionCN: 手机；在日常口语中比 handset 更常用

entries.definition: a phone with no cable between base and handset
entries.definitionCN: 无绳电话；基座与手持部分之间没有电线

normalIntro.en: Handset is literally the set you hold in your hand when you talk on the phone.
normalIntro.cn: handset 字面就是「用手拿的一套东西」，也就是打电话时握在手里的部分。

normal.en: Hand plus set: a set made for the hand to hold.
normal.cn: hand 加 set：专为手握而造的一套装置。

normal.en: Pick up and put down are the classic verbs with handset.
normal.cn: pick up 与 put down 是与 handset 最经典的动词搭配。

normal.en: Cordless handset and mobile handset show the word applied to the whole phone.
normal.cn: cordless handset 与 mobile handset 说明这个词也可指整部电话。

normal.en: Keep it apart from hashtag, which is a different compound entirely.
normal.cn: 把它与 hashtag 区分开，两者是完全不同的复合词。

normal.en: In Britain a mobile is the everyday word; handset is more formal or technical.
normal.cn: 在英国日常说 mobile，handset 偏正式或偏技术。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy black earpiece in a curved hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只弯起的手握着重重的黑色听筒。

abstract.en: Think of a finger lifting the earpiece off its cradle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指把听筒从底座上挑起。

abstract.en: See a small cordless unit resting in a stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一部无绳话机静静躺在支架上。

examples.en: He placed the handset gently back on the desk phone.
examples.cn: 他把听筒轻轻放回桌面电话上。

examples.en: People now replace their handsets far more often than before.
examples.cn: 如今的低价手机，摄像头比五年前的贵价手机还好。

examples.en: Please check that the handset is fully charged before the shift.
examples.cn: 请在交班前确认话机已充满电。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「汉德塞特」——「汉」子把听筒「塞」到耳边，特别小心地通话；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 hand（手）+ set（一套装置）→ handset（供手持的电话听筒）→ 泛指无绳话机、手机等手持通话设备，核心义「手握的一套装置」。

sensesIntro.en: Handset starts as the held earpiece of a telephone, then shifts to the whole cordless or mobile phone, and then to any hand-held remote unit.
sensesIntro.cn: handset 起初指电话上手持的听筒，继而指整部无绳电话或手机，最后泛指任何手持的遥控部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a telephone earpiece close to the ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着电话听筒贴在耳边。

branches.en: The earpiece is the original and still literal sense.
branches.cn: 听筒是最初的、仍然字面的义项。

branches.en: A cordless or mobile phone is the whole set you hold.
branches.cn: 无绳电话或手机就是整件手持装置。

branches.en: Other machines also ship with a small hand-held control.
branches.cn: 其他机器也会配一个小型手持控制件。

branches.en: Both senses describe what the hand grips while the person talks.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述人在通话时手里握着的东西。

branches.en: Both are small sets made to be operated in one hand.
branches.cn: 两者都是用一只手操作的小型装置。

intro.en: Handset is English hand plus set, with handset maker and the parallel headset and hand-held built on the same hand image.
intro.cn: handset 由英语 hand 与 set 组合而成，handset maker 以及平行的 headset、hand-held 都建立在同一个「手」的意象上。

latinIntro.en: Handset has no Latin source of its own; set reached English through Old French from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: handset 本身没有拉丁语来源，只是其中的 set 经古法语来自拉丁语。

items.example: Hand supplies the held-in-the-hand image.
items.exampleCN: hand 提供「握在手中」的意象。

items.example: Set means a unit of matched parts.
items.exampleCN: set 指一套配套的部件。

items.meaning: a telephone part or phone held by hand
items.example: Handset names what the hand holds while calling.
items.exampleCN: handset 指通话时手握着的东西。

items.meaningCN: 头戴式耳机麦克风组合
items.example: Headset copies the pattern with head.
items.exampleCN: headset 用 head 套用了同样的构词。

items.meaning: a small unit worn at the ear
items.example: Earset shifts the worn part to the ear.
items.exampleCN: earset 把佩戴部位换到了耳朵。

items.meaning: small enough to hold in the hand
items.example: Hand-held devices need light batteries.
items.exampleCN: 手持设备需要轻便的电池。

items.example: The handset maker reported record sales.
items.exampleCN: 这家手机制造商报告了创纪录的销量。

items.example: A cordless handset can be used around the house.
items.exampleCN: 无绳话机可以在屋里到处使用。

items.example: The suffix -s forms handsets.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 handsets。

items.example: The shop sells refurbished units at low prices.
items.exampleCN: 这家店出售翻新机。

latinEntries.example: Sedere underlies the idea of a thing placed in position.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sedere 是「放置到位」这一概念的来源。
sette 进入英语后变成 set。

definition_zh: 偶然的；随意的；漫无计划的；杂乱无章的；偶然地；杂乱
definition_en: happening by chance rather than by plan, and therefore often careless or untidy
core_image: 一把骰子随手撒在桌上，落到哪里算哪里
scene: 书架上堆满没有分类的旧书，桌角的咖啡渍边缘粘着几张便签。Papers on the desk lay in a haphazard pile that no one had arranged for years.
sceneCN: 这里 haphazard 是「随意堆放的；杂乱无章的」（第 3 个义项：没有安排布置、凌乱无序）；句意：桌上的文件随意堆成一摞，多年来没人整理过。

pos.zh: 偶然的；随意的；杂乱无章的

collocations.zh: 随意的方式；杂乱无章的做法

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，表示「随意地；杂乱地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，指「随意、无章法」的性质
构成 haphazard 的另一半，本义是「骰子游戏」，现代义为「危险；隐患」

senses.title: Driven by mere chance
senses.definition: happening by chance rather than through any plan or design
senses.definitionCN: 出于偶然而非事先安排才发生的
senses.example: Their meeting was completely haphazard, a chance turn in a crowded station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相遇完全是偶然，只是在拥挤的车站里转错了一个弯。
senses.why: Chance came first: the old phrase meant by the dice game, and the game stood for luck itself.
senses.whyCN: 偶然是第一层意思：旧说法「靠掷骰游戏」里，骰子游戏就是运气的代名词。

senses.title: Acting without method
senses.definition: done in a careless way, with no fixed order or clear method
senses.definitionCN: 做事粗疏随意，没有固定次序或明确方法
senses.example: The search was haphazard, so the rescue team covered the same ground twice.
senses.exampleCN: 搜救毫无章法，救援队把同一片区域搜了两遍。
senses.why: Once a person relies on luck, the next step is to drop the method and act in whatever order comes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个人依赖运气，下一步就是丢掉方法，抓到什么按什么顺序做。

senses.title: Untidily arranged
senses.definition: arranged in a disordered way, with no careful thought about where things go
senses.definitionCN: 物品摆放凌乱无序，没有认真考虑过位置
senses.example: Books and papers were stacked in a haphazard heap beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 书和文件在门边堆成一团，凌乱不堪。
senses.why: No method in the doing leaves no order in the placing, so the word spreads from actions to objects.
senses.whyCN: 做事没有方法，摆放自然没有秩序，于是这个词从行为又蔓延到物品。

senses.title: Unreliable because random
senses.definition: so random in making or doing that results are uneven and cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 因凭运气行事而成果参差不齐、不可信赖
senses.example: Haphazard sampling gave the survey a large margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 随意抽样使这项调查产生了很大的误差。
senses.why: A random process cannot be repeated, so its results vary and lose the reliability a planned process would give.
senses.whyCN: 随机的过程无法重复，结果便忽高忽低，失掉了有计划的过程才有的可靠性。

senses.title: Grown up without planning
senses.definition: having developed gradually through accidental steps instead of deliberate design
senses.definitionCN: 不是刻意设计，而是一步步碰巧累积发展而成
senses.example: The old town grew in a haphazard pattern of crooked lanes.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城沿着歪斜的小巷杂乱地生长成形。
senses.why: Countless unplanned choices, repeated over a long time, pile up into a shape nobody designed.
senses.whyCN: 无数未经计划的决定在漫长时间里层层累积，长成了没人设计过的形态。

senses.title: In a random manner
senses.definition: in a way that follows chance rather than order or plan
senses.definitionCN: 以听凭偶然、不按次序或计划的方式
senses.example: The crates were piled haphazardly along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 木箱被随意地堆在墙边。
senses.why: The adverb simply takes the adjective and asks in what manner the action was done.
senses.whyCN: 副词形式只是把形容词接过来，回答「以什么方式」完成这个动作。

intro.en: Haphazard joins old English hap, which means chance or luck, with hazard, a name for a dice game taken from French.
intro.cn: haphazard 由中古英语 hap（机遇、运气）和从法语借入的 hazard（一种掷骰游戏）复合而成，两个字都在强调「碰运气」。

items.en: Old English hap meant chance or fortune, a close cousin of happen.
items.cn: 古英语的 hap 意为机遇、运气，与 happen 是近亲。

items.en: French hasard named a dice game; its deeper source is uncertain, though Arabic roots have been proposed.
items.cn: 法语 hasard 指一种掷骰游戏；更早的来源不确定，有学者提出可能与阿拉伯语有关，仅为假说。

items.en: Middle English adopted hazard with the sense of a game of chance.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 hazard，指凭运气的骰子游戏。

items.en: Hazard also came to mean a risk or a source of danger.
items.cn: hazard 随后又引申为风险、危险的来源。

items.en: At an inflection it could mean by game of chance, and haphazard grew from that phrase.
items.cn: at hazard 一度表示「靠掷骰游戏来决定」，haphazard 正是从这个说法里长出来的。

items.en: Haphazard became an adjective for anything left to luck instead of order.
items.cn: haphazard 成为形容词，指一切听凭运气而不讲条理的事物。

note.en: Haphazard shares its second half with hazard, and on the meaning side it sits close to random and random synonyms.
note.cn: haphazard 的后半截与 hazard 同源，意义上一方面与 random 等表示随机的词相邻，一方面又与原义 hazard 相连。

entries.definition: danger or risk, from a game of chance
entries.definitionCN: 危险；风险，本义为靠运气的骰子游戏

entries.definition: in a careless, unordered way
entries.definitionCN: 随意地；杂乱地

entries.definition: the quality of being disorderly or left to chance
entries.definitionCN: 随意、无章法的性质

entries.definition: chosen or happening without a pattern
entries.definitionCN: 随机的；无规律的

entries.definition: untidy or lacking control
entries.definitionCN: 混乱的；无秩序的

entries.definition: not following a fixed method
entries.definitionCN: 不系统的

normalIntro.en: Haphazard is a plain compound: hap for luck plus hazard for the dice, so its parts spell out chance.
normalIntro.cn: haphazard 是明明白白的复合词：hap 表运气，hazard 表骰子游戏，两个部件合起来就是「全靠运气」。

normal.en: Split it as hap and hazard, and note that hap survives in happen and hapless.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 hap 与 hazard；hap 至今还活在 happen 与 hapless 里。

normal.en: The adverb haphazardly is the most common everyday form in writing.
normal.cn: 副词 haphazardly 是写作中最常见的日常形式。

normal.en: Verb plus way or manner is the usual frame: a haphazard way of working.
normal.cn: 常见框架是动词加 way 或 manner，如 a haphazard way of working。

normal.en: Contrast hazard, which names a danger, with haphazard, which names a lack of order.
normal.cn: 对比 hazard（危险事物）与 haphazard（缺乏条理）：一个指险，一个指乱。

normal.en: The adjective rarely comes before a person; it describes actions, layouts, and methods.
normal.cn: 这个形容词很少修饰人，主要修饰行为、布局和方法。

abstract.en: Picture dice thrown onto a table: nobody aims, and wherever each cube falls is the result.
abstract.cn: 想象把骰子往桌上一撒：没人瞄准，骰子落在哪儿就是哪儿。

abstract.en: Picture a workman who grabs any tool within reach instead of following a list.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工人不按清单来，手边摸到什么工具就用什么。

abstract.en: Picture a heap of books that has never once been sorted by title.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆书，从来没有按书名排过一次。

examples.en: The shelves were filled in a haphazard order, so nothing could be found quickly.
examples.cn: 书架上的东西随意摆放，所以要找什么都快不起来。

examples.en: Their travel plans were haphazard and changed every morning.
examples.cn: 他们的旅行计划很随意，每天早上都在变。

examples.en: What began as haphazard notes on napkins became a published history.
examples.cn: 起初只是餐巾纸上随手记下的零散笔记，后来竟成了一部出版的史书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈泼哈扎德」：随手一泼，又随手一扎，东西东倒西歪，毫无章法；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 hap（机遇、运气）＋ hazard（源自法语的掷骰游戏）→ haphazard，核心义「听凭运气、不按计划」，再引申为「杂乱无章」。

sensesIntro.en: From the dice game the word first names what happens by chance, then how carelessly people act, then how untidily things are arranged, and finally what is unreliably uneven.
sensesIntro.cn: haphazard 从掷骰游戏出发，先指偶然发生的事，再指做事马虎无方法，接着指摆放杂乱，最后指因随意而致结果不可靠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dice tossed onto a table, landing wherever chance decides.
core.cn: 核心意象：骰子随手撒在桌上，落在哪里全凭运气。

branches.en: Chance is the oldest layer, inherited from hap and the dice game.
branches.cn: 偶然是最古老的一层，承自 hap 与掷骰游戏。

branches.en: Left to luck, a person stops following a method.
branches.cn: 一旦听凭运气，做事的人就不再依据方法。

branches.en: No method easily becomes no order in the objects around us.
branches.cn: 没有方法很容易变成周围物品的没有秩序。

branches.en: Careless method makes results uneven and hard to rely on.
branches.cn: 马虎的方法让结果参差不齐，难以信赖。

branches.en: Chance steps, repeated for centuries, shape towns no one planned.
branches.cn: 无数偶然的步子重复上几百年，就塑造出无人规划的小镇。

intro.en: Haphazard is a compound whose two halves each carry the idea of chance, with the adverb and noun formed by -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: haphazard 是复合词，两个部件都带有「碰运气」的意思；副词与名词分别由 -ly 和 -ness 构成。

latinIntro.en: The first element hap is native English; the second half hazard entered through French and has no certain Latin origin.
latinIntro.cn: 前半 hap 是本土英语词；后半 hazard 经由法语进入英语，其拉丁语来源并无定论。

items.example: Hap survives today mainly inside compound words.
items.exampleCN: hap 今天主要活在一些复合词里。

items.meaning: a game of dice, later a risk
items.meaningCN: 掷骰游戏，后来指引出风险
items.example: Hazard supplies the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: hazard 提供这个词的后半部分。

items.example: Haphazard was first used for what happens at hazard.
items.exampleCN: haphazard 最初用来指「在偶然中发生的事」。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成副词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly turns haphazard into an adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 haphazard 变成方式副词。

items.meaning: in a random or careless way
items.example: Haphazardly is common in written descriptions.
items.exampleCN: haphazardly 在书面描写中很常见。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成抽象名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness gives the quality noun haphazardness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 造出表示性质的名词 haphazardness。

items.example: Haphazardness describes a lack of system.
items.exampleCN: haphazardness 描述缺乏系统的状态。

items.meaningCN: 偶然；随意之举（罕见用词）
items.example: The rare noun haphazardry appears mainly in older texts.
items.exampleCN: 罕见名词 haphazardry 主要见于较旧的文本。

items.example: The adverb often modifies the phrase haphazardly done.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词常修饰「随意完成的」这一说法。

latinEntries.example: French hazard came through Old French hasard.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hazard 经由古法语 hasard 传入英语。
